It covers every breaking change, maps each v1 endpoint to its v2 replacement, and provides before/after examples you can adapt directly.\n\n**Sources.** The v2 material in this guide reflects the reconciled TaskFlow API v2 documentation (see `taskflow_api_v2_docs.md`), the OpenAPI 3.0 specification (version 2.0.1), and the documented discrepancy report. Where the sources disagreed, the specification was treated as the source of truth.\n\n## Overview of what changed\n\nv2 is a substantial revision. The changes fall into four groups:\n\n1. **Breaking changes** — things that will make v1 integrations fail (authentication headers, endpoint paths, field names, pagination, timestamps, error format, the assign verb).\n2. **Changed behavior** — things that still work but behave differently (deleting projects, search scope, validation strictness).\n3. **New capabilities** — things v1 could not do at all (label filters, watchers, MFA login flow, webhook signing, richer user roles).\n4. **Known inconsistencies** — residual issues in the v2 platform that you should code defensively around.\n\n## Deprecation timeline\n\nNo formal v1 end-of-life date is published in the available materials. Plan your migration without assuming a hard cutoff, and contact `support@taskflow.io` for your tenant's v1 retirement schedule if you need one.\n\n## Quick reference: breaking changes\n\n| Area | v1 | v2 |\n|------|----|----|\n| Base URL | `https://api.taskflow.io/api` | `https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2` |\n| Authentication | `X-API-Key: <key>` header | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |\n| List pagination | `limit`, `offset` | `page`, `per_page` (+ `meta` object) |\n| Timestamps | Unix seconds | ISO 8601 (two exceptions, see below) |\n| Error body | `{\"error\": \"message\"}` | Structured error envelope |\n| Assign a task | `PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign` | `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign` |\n| Task description field | `desc` | `description` |\n| Task due date field | `deadline` (Unix timestamp) | `due_date` (ISO 8601 date-time) |\n| Task assignee field | `assigned_to` | `assignee_id` |\n| Task project field | `project` | `project_id` |\n| Comments & history | Dedicated endpoints | `include` query parameter on task retrieval |\n| Search | `GET /api/search` (tasks and projects) | `GET /search/tasks` (tasks only) |\n| Organization field on user | `org` | `organization_id` |\n| Webhook events | 4 events | 10 declared events (+2 observed, see below) |\n| Rate limit | 60 requests/minute | 100/minute (free), 1000/minute (paid) |\n\n## Base URL\n\nAll v2 requests go to a versioned base URL. Update the base URL in your client first — nothing from v1 resolves under v2 paths.\n\n```\nv1: https://api.taskflow.io/api/tasks\nv2: https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks\n```\n\n## Authentication\n\nv1 used a static key sent in an `X-API-Key` header. v2 uses Bearer authentication:\n\n```\nAuthorization: Bearer <token>\n```\n\nThere are two paths to a valid v2 credential:\n\n- **API keys** — generate a key from the TaskFlow dashboard under *Settings > API Keys* and send it as a Bearer token. This is the closest equivalent to the v1 flow.\n- **User tokens** — v2 adds first-class authentication endpoints that v1 never had:\n  - `POST /auth/login` with `email` and `password` obtains a token. If the account has multi-factor authentication enabled, the API returns `403` with an indication that MFA is required; retry with an `mfa_code` included.\n  - `POST /auth/refresh` exchanges a refresh token for a new access token. Build token refresh into your client if you use this flow.\n\nNote that `/auth/login` is intentionally open (no Bearer header required) — this is a change from v1, where \"all API calls require an API key.\"\n\n## Endpoint mapping\n\n| v1 endpoint | v2 endpoint | Notes |\n|-------------|-------------|-------|\n| `GET /api/tasks` | `GET /tasks` | Parameter changes, see [pagination](#pagination) and [filters](#new-filter-and-sort-options). |\n| `POST /api/tasks` | `POST /tasks` | Body field renames; returns `201 Created` (v1 returned `200 OK`). |\n| `GET /api/tasks/:id` | `GET /tasks/{taskId}` | Supports `include=comments,history,attachments`. |\n| `PUT /api/tasks/:id` | `PUT /tasks/{taskId}` | Same verb; body field renames; may return `409`. |\n| `DELETE /api/tasks/:id` | `DELETE /tasks/{taskId}` | Permission check returns `403` when insufficient. |\n| `PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign` | `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign` | **Verb changed.** Body field renamed `user_id` → `assignee_id`. |\n| `GET /api/tasks/:id/comments` | `GET /tasks/{taskId}?include=comments` | No longer a separate endpoint. |\n| `POST /api/tasks/:id/comments` | *No direct v2 equivalent in the specification* | Reading comments moved to `include`; there is no documented v2 comment-creation endpoint — see [removed and folded endpoints](#removed-and-folded-endpoints). |\n| `GET /api/tasks/:id/history` | `GET /tasks/{taskId}?include=history` | No longer a separate endpoint. |\n| `GET /api/projects` | `GET /projects` | Now paginated; supports `archived` and `role` filters. |\n| `POST /api/projects` | `POST /projects` | `desc` → `description`; new `template_id` and `visibility` fields; returns `201`. |\n| `DELETE /api/projects/:id` | `DELETE /projects/{projectId}` | New `cascade` parameter; see [project deletion](#project-deletion). |\n| `GET /api/users/current` | `GET /users/me` | `org` → `organization_id`; supports a `fields` parameter. |\n| `GET /api/search` | `GET /search/tasks` | Tasks only; the `type` parameter is gone; filter by `project_id`. |\n| `POST /api/webhooks` | `POST /webhooks` | New `secret` and `active` fields; expanded event list; returns `201`. |\n| `GET /api/webhooks` | *No v2 equivalent in the specification* | No list-webhooks operation is defined in the v2 spec — see [removed and folded endpoints](#removed-and-folded-endpoints). |\n| `DELETE /api/webhooks/:id` | `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}` | Path parameter renamed; returns `204 No Content`. |\n| — | `GET /projects/{projectId}`, `PUT /projects/{projectId}` | **New in v2**: retrieve and update a single project (v1 only supported create, list, and delete). |\n| — | `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh` | **New in v2**: token-based authentication. |\n\n## Field renames\n\nRename these fields in every request body and every place you read responses:\n\n| Object | v1 field | v2 field |\n|--------|----------|----------|\n| Task | `desc` | `description` |\n| Task | `deadline` (Unix timestamp) | `due_date` (ISO 8601) |\n| Task | `assigned_to` | `assignee_id` |\n| Task | `project` | `project_id` |\n| User | `org` | `organization_id` |\n| Assign request body | `user_id` | `assignee_id` |\n| List filters | `project` (query parameter) | `project_id` |\n\n## Timestamps\n\nv1 documented \"all timestamps are Unix.\" v2 standardizes on **ISO 8601** date-time strings (for example, `2024-03-15T00:00:00Z`). This affects `deadline` → `due_date` above, task history entries, and project timestamps.\n\n**Known exceptions.** Two response fields still return Unix timestamps in v2: `projects.created` and `users.last_login`. This inconsistency is recorded in the discrepancy report. Parse these two fields defensively (numeric epoch versus ISO string) until the platform standardizes them.\n\nWhen sending `due_date`, supply a full ISO 8601 value with a UTC offset; values without an offset are interpreted as UTC.\n\n## Pagination\n\nv1 list endpoints used `limit`/`offset`. v2 uses `page`/`per_page` and returns a `meta` object with pagination information:\n\n```\nv1: GET /api/tasks?limit=50&offset=100\nv2: GET /api/v2/tasks?page=3&per_page=50\n```\n\n- Defaults per the specification: `page` starts at 1, `per_page` defaults to **25** with a **maximum of 200**. If you requested large pages in v1, split them into multiple v2 requests.\n- **Projects are now paginated.** v1 returned all projects in a single response, and the current v2 documentation still claims the projects endpoint is unpaginated — the specification defines `page`/`per_page` for it, and the specification wins. If your integration assumed \"one response contains every project,\" rework it to follow the `meta` object.\n\n## Errors\n\nv1 returned a flat body:\n\n```json\n{ \"error\": \"message\" }\n```\n\nv2 returns a structured envelope:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"code\": \"VALIDATION_ERROR\",\n    \"message\": \"...\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nMigrate error handling to read `error.code` and `error.message`. **Caution:** some older v2 endpoints may still return the flat legacy format; the platform is standardizing across routes. Handle both shapes during your migration window:\n\n```python\ndef error_code(body):\n    err = body.get(\"error\", {})\n    return err[\"code\"] if isinstance(err, dict) else err\n```\n\nNew status codes to handle that v1 did not document: `409 Conflict` (stale concurrent task update — re-fetch and retry), `422 Unprocessable Entity` (validation failures, such as a title longer than 200 characters), and `429 Too Many Requests` (rate limiting).\n\n## Assigning a task\n\nThe assign endpoint changed both verb and body:\n\n```\nv1: PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign    body: {\"user_id\": 93}\nv2: POST /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}/assign    body: {\"assignee_id\": 93}\n```\n\nBehavior notes:\n\n- Assigning a new assignee **replaces** any existing assignment.\n- By default the assignee is notified; pass `\"notify\": false` to suppress the notification.\n- To unassign, send `\"assignee_id\": null` via the task update endpoint (`PUT /tasks/{taskId}`), which v2 documents as the unassignment path.\n\n## Removed and folded endpoints\n\nTwo v1 endpoints have **no v2 equivalent in the specification**, and two were folded into other operations:\n\n- **`POST /api/tasks/:id/comments`** — v2 reads comments via `GET /tasks/{taskId}?include=comments`, but the specification defines no operation to create a comment. If your integration posts comments, contact TaskFlow support for the supported v2 path before migrating; do not assume the v1 endpoint keeps working under the v2 base URL.\n- **`GET /api/webhooks`** — v2 lets you create (`POST /webhooks`) and delete (`DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}`) webhooks, but defines no list operation. Track your webhook IDs on your side.\n- **`GET /api/tasks/:id/comments`** and **`GET /api/tasks/:id/history`** — replaced by the `include` query parameter on `GET /tasks/{taskId}`. Multiple expansions can be combined: `?include=comments,history`.\n\n## Search\n\nv1 search spanned tasks and projects:\n\n```\nv1: GET /api/search?q=launch&type=task\nv2: GET /api/v2/search/tasks?q=launch&project_id=12\n```\n\n- The `type` parameter is gone — v2 search is task-scoped. If you searched projects, use the project list endpoint with its filters instead.\n- `project_id` narrows search to a single project.\n- Update the path (`/search/tasks` under the v2 base URL).\n\n## Project deletion\n\nv1 deleted all tasks in a project implicitly. v2 keeps that default but makes it explicit and controllable:\n\n- `DELETE /projects/{projectId}` cascades by default (`cascade=true`): all tasks in the project are deleted. Observable behavior matches v1, but now each deleted task also emits a `task.deleted` webhook event.\n- Pass `?cascade=false` to require an empty project; deleting a project that still contains tasks then returns `409 Conflict`.\n\n## Filters, sorting, and expanded fields\n\nNew capabilities with no v1 counterpart — optional to adopt, useful to know about:\n\n- **Task filters**: filter by `label`; the `status` filter now also accepts `blocked`; sort with `sort=created_at|updated_at|priority|due_date` and `order=asc|desc`.\n- **Task creation**: pass `watchers` (array of user IDs), `tags` (array of strings), and `priority: urgent` (new value; the enum is `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`, `urgent`).\n- **Project creation**: pass `template_id` to create from a template and `visibility` to control project visibility.\n- **Project filters**: `archived=true` includes archived projects; `role` filters by member role, which now includes a `viewer` role.\n- **User profile**: `GET /users/me?fields=id,email,name` trims the response to selected fields.\n- **Task retrieval**: `include=comments,history,attachments` expands related resources in one request, replacing v1's separate round-trips.\n\n## Webhooks\n\nThe event catalog grew from 4 events in v1 to **10 subscribable events** in v2:\n\n`task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `task.assigned`, `task.commented`, `project.created`, `project.archived`, `project.deleted`, `member.added`, `member.removed`\n\nAdditional v2 webhook changes:\n\n- Registration (`POST /webhooks`) accepts an optional `secret` for HMAC payload verification — verify signatures server-side before trusting payloads.\n- An `active` flag (default `true`) lets you pause a subscription without deleting it.\n- **Undocumented events exist**: production emits `task.due_date_approaching` and `task.overdue`, which are not in the `events` enum. Do not build critical logic on them until they are added to the specification. See the webhook event catalog for full details, including delivery-retry semantics (failed deliveries are retried 3 times, then marked permanently failed).\n\n## Rate limits\n\n| Tier | v1 | v2 |\n|------|----|----|\n| Free | 60 requests/minute | 100 requests/minute |\n| Paid | 60 requests/minute | 1000 requests/minute |\n\nOn limit, v2 returns `429 Too Many Requests`; read the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` response header to throttle proactively. Most integrations migrated from 60/min to 100/min need no changes, but paid-tier integrations that previously self-throttled can safely raise their throughput.\n\n## Validation strictness\n\nv2 enforces limits that v1 left undefined. If your integration creates tasks, check:\n\n- `title` is required and limited to **200 characters** (a 201-character title returns `422`).\n- Enum values are validated — an invalid `status`, `priority`, or unknown `assignee_id` returns `422`.\n- Concurrent update conflicts return `409`; re-fetch the task and retry rather than blindly resending the update.\n\n## Before/after examples\n\n### List tasks (pagination and filters)\n\n```bash\n# v1\ncurl -s -H \"X-API-Key: $TASKFLOW_KEY\" \\\n  \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/tasks?status=open&project=12&limit=50&offset=0\"\n\n# v2\ncurl -s --fail \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer $TASKFLOW_TOKEN\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks?status=open&project_id=12&page=1&per_page=50\"\n```\n\n### Create a task\n\n```bash\n# v1\ncurl -s -X POST -H \"X-API-Key: $TASKFLOW_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\"title\":\"Ship release\",\"desc\":\"Final checks\",\"project\":12,\"assigned_to\":93,\"deadline\":1710460800}' \\\n  \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/tasks\"\n\n# v2\ncurl -s --fail -X POST \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer reasoning_content:
Now the migration guide. Structure planned earlier. Let me write it — grounded in v1 doc (read fully), spec, current v2 docs, and my own rewrite. Keep before/after cURL examples accurate.

Key v1 facts (from v1 doc):
- Base: https://api.taskflow.io/api
- Auth: X-API-Key header
- GET /api/tasks — params status, project, limit, offset; returns array
- POST /api/tasks — body: title (req), desc, status, priority, assigned_to, project, deadline (Unix); returns 200 OK
- GET /api/tasks/:id
- PUT /api/tasks/:id — send only what changed
- DELETE /api/tasks/:id — must be owner
- GET /api/projects — list all
- POST /api/projects — name (req), desc
- GET /api/users/current — id, email, name, role, org
- GET /api/tasks/:id/comments, POST /api/tasks/:id/comments (body: text)
- GET /api/search — q, type (task or project)
- PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign — body user_id; "convenience endpoint; can also update assigned_to directly"
- GET /api/tasks/:id/history — old/new value, who, when Unix
- DELETE /api/projects/:id — deletes all tasks too
- Errors: {"error": "message"}; 400, 401, 404, 500
- Webhooks: POST /api/webhooks (url, events), GET /api/webhooks, DELETE /api/webhooks/:id; 4 events
- Rate limit 60 req/min; all timestamps Unix

v2 facts:
- Base: https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2
- Auth: Bearer (docs) + /auth/login (email, password, mfa_code → 403 when MFA required) + /auth/refresh
- Tasks: status enum + blocked; priority + urgent; sort incl due_date; project_id filter; label filter; page/per_page (default 25, max 200 per spec); meta in response
- Create task: title max 200 (spec), due_date ISO 8601, watchers, template_id?, notify... (my rewrite: watchers yes; template_id is on project create)
- Retrieve task: include=comments,history,attachments
- Update task: PUT, partial; 409 on concurrent modification
- Delete task: permissions → 403
- Assign: POST, assignee_id, notify (default true), reassignment replaces
- Projects: paginated page/per_page + meta (spec) — despite docs claiming none; archived filter; role filter incl viewer; create with template_id, visibility
- Retrieve/update project (new vs v1 docs); delete with cascade (default true — same observable behavior as v1)
- Users: GET /users/me, fields param, organization_id; users.last_login remains Unix timestamp
- Search: GET /search/tasks?q=&project_id=...; type param gone
- Webhooks: POST /webhooks (url, events 10, secret, active) → 201; DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId} → 204; no list endpoint in spec
- Errors: structured envelope; legacy flat on some endpoints; 422 validation
- Rate: 100/min free, 1000/min paid; 429 + X-RateLimit-Remaining
- Webhook events now 10 declared + 2 observed

I need to be careful about details I reference from the spec that I haven't re-verified since compaction: e.g., sort values, label param, per_page 25/200, meta object. Let me quickly verify the /tasks GET params and meta from the spec to avoid errors in before/after examples.

[{"content": "## Goal

1. **Discrepancy report (CSV)** — cross-referencing the OpenAPI 3.0 YAML spec against current Markdown docs, incorporating signals from the audit tracker beyond simple diff.
2. **API documentation style guide (Markdown, ≥1500 words)** — governing all future TaskFlow API docs, grounded in local references + GitLab's REST API documentation guidelines (pinned snapshot; no internet).
3. **Complete rewritten TaskFlow API v2 docs (Markdown)** — every endpoint conforming to the style guide, incorporating everything the spec knows that docs don't, resolving every audit-tracker issue.
4. **Webhook event catalog (HTML)** — synthesizing spec-declared events with production-log-observed events; each entry documents event name, description, trigger condition, example payload, and provenance across both sources.
5. **v1-to-v2 migration guide (Markdown)** — developer-facing, using legacy v1 docs + reconciled v2 materials.

## Instructions

- **Source files** (in `/work/task_folder/`): `TASK_INSTRUCTIONS.txt`, `doc_audit_tracker.csv` (18 endpoint audit rows with priority/status/notes), `restapidocs_combined_template.md` (RESTAPIDocs template), `taskflow_api_docs_current.md` (v2 docs), `taskflow_api_docs_current_v1.md`, `taskflow_openapi_v2_extract.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.0.3, version 2.0.1), `webhook_delivery_log.json`. ## Discoveries

**Key spec-vs-docs discrepancies found (45 recorded, D-001 to D-045):**
- **8 operations entirely missing from current v2 docs** (exist in spec): `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /projects/{projectId}`, `POST /webhooks`, `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}`, `GET /search/tasks`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`.
- Schema deltas: status enum missing `blocked`; priority missing `urgent`; sort missing `due_date`; role missing `viewer`; `label`, `include`, `fields`, `watchers`, `template_id`, `visibility`, `cascade`, `notify` params undocumented; `title` maxLength 255 (docs) vs 200 (spec); `per_page` default 20/max 100 (docs) vs 25/200 (spec).

- Global: version 2.0 vs 2.0.1; docs say "all API calls require API key" but spec has open endpoint `/auth/login`; two conflicting error formats (structured envelope is canonical, flat shape legacy); Unix timestamps (`projects.created`, `users.last_login`) inconsistent with ISO 8601.

- **Retry evidence**: delivery `d-90008` (`project.deleted`) returned 502 with `retry_attempts: 3`, `final_status: failed` → documented retry policy (3 attempts, backoff, then marked failed).

**Environment constraint:** Writing to `/tmp` is blocked by an `external_directory` deny rule. Created `/work/.tmp_build/gen_discrepancy_csv.py` as a Python generator (needed because hand-written CSV had comma-in-value quoting bugs). **Cleanup of `/work/.tmp_build/` still pending.**

Covers source-of-truth hierarchy (spec > docs > audit tracker > production evidence), page structure, GitLab-style verb tables, attribute table rules, cURL/JSON example conventions, error/status codes, cross-cutting conventions (auth, pagination, rate limiting, ISO 8601 timestamps, webhooks), terminology table, deprecation handling, review checklist mapped to audit tracker columns.
- ✅ **`/work/output/taskflow_api_v2_docs.md`** — just written. Full rewrite covering all 16 operations: auth (login w/ mfa_code + 403 MFA, refresh), tasks (list w/ label/blocked/25/200/due_date, create w/ watchers/urgent/maxLength 200, retrieve w/ include, update w/ 409 + response example, delete w/ permissions, assign w/ notify + reassignment semantics), projects (list w/ pagination + viewer, create w/ template_id/visibility, retrieve/update/delete w/ cascade), users/me w/ fields param, search/tasks, webhooks (create w/ 10 events + HMAC secret + retry policy notes, delete). Uses YAML front matter, metadata blocks (URL/Method/Auth/Permissions), request/response attribute tables, cURL examples with long options, error tables, Notes sections.
- ⏳ **`/work/output/webhook_event_catalog.html`** — **NOT yet written**. 1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.
102: 
103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## DELETE /api/projects/:id
114: 
115: Delete a project. All tasks in the project will also be deleted.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Errors
120: 
121: Errors return JSON: `{"error": "message"}`.
122: 
123: Common codes: 400, 401, 404, 500.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Webhooks
128: 
129: POST /api/webhooks - register a webhook. Body: `url`, `events` (array).
130: 
131: GET /api/webhooks - list webhooks.
132: 
133: DELETE /api/webhooks/:id - remove a webhook.
134: 
135: Events: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `project.created`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## Notes
140: 
141: - Rate limit: 60 req/min.
142: - All timestamps are Unix.
143: - Contact support@taskflow.io for help.

(End of file - total 143 lines)

# TaskFlow API Documentation

**Version**: 2.0
**Last Updated**: March 2024

Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.

## Authentication

All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
```

You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

---

## Tasks

### GET /api/v2/tasks

Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.

**Query Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |

TaskFlow API — Webhook Event Catalog

\n

\n This catalog lists every webhook event the TaskFlow platform emits, combining two sources:\n the events declared as subscribable values in the OpenAPI 3.0 specification\n (taskflow_openapi_v2_extract.yaml, API version 2.0.1) and the events actually observed\n in a production delivery log (webhook_delivery_log.json, export dated 2024-03-10).\n

1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.
102: 
103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## DELETE /api/projects/:id
114: 
115: Delete a project. All tasks in the project will also be deleted.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Errors
120: 
121: Errors return JSON: `{"error": "message"}`.
122: 
123: Common codes: 400, 401, 404, 500.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Webhooks
128: 
129: POST /api/webhooks - register a webhook. Body: `url`, `events` (array).
130: 
131: GET /api/webhooks - list webhooks.
132: 
133: DELETE /api/webhooks/:id - remove a webhook.
134: 
135: Events: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `project.created`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## Notes
140: 
141: - Rate limit: 60 req/min.
142: - All timestamps are Unix.
143: - Contact support@taskflow.io for help.

# TaskFlow API Documentation

**Version**: 2.0
**Last Updated**: March 2024

Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.

## Authentication

All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
```

You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

---

## Tasks

### GET /api/v2/tasks

Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.

**Query Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |

treat as undocumented until the\n    spec is updated (see <a href=\"#gaps\">Known gaps</a>).\n  </p>\n</section>\n\n<section id=\"catalog\">\n  <h2>Event catalog</h2>\n\n  <h3>Task events</h3>\n\n  <article class=\"event\" id=\"task-created\">\n    <header><h3>task.created</h3><span class=\"badge spec-prod\">Spec + Production</span></header>\n    <dl>\n      <dt>Description</dt><dd>Fired when a new task is created in a project.</dd>\n      <dt>Trigger</dt><dd>Successful <code>POST /tasks</code>.</dd>\n    </dl>\n    <pre>{\n  \"event\": \"task.created\",\n  \"task_id\": 1042,\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}</pre>\n    <p class=\"obs\">Observed in production: delivery <code>d-90001</code>, 2024-03-01T14:22:00Z, HTTP 200.</p>\n  </article>\n\n  <article class=\"event\" id=\"task-updated\">\n    <header><h3>task.updated</h3><span class=\"badge spec-prod\">Spec + Production</span></header>\n    <dl>\n      <dt>Description</dt><dd>Fired when one or more fields of an existing task change. Includes the owning <code>project_id</code> so consumers can clean up project-scoped state.</dd>\n      <dt>Trigger</dt><dd>Successful <code>DELETE /tasks/{taskId}</code>, or deletion of a task via project cascade.</dd>\n    </dl>\n    <pre>{\n  \"event\": \"task.deleted\",\n  \"task_id\": 999,\n  \"project_id\": 3,\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}</pre>\n    <p class=\"obs\">Observed in production: delivery <code>d-90010</code>, 2024-03-08T09:00:00Z, HTTP 200.</p>\n  </article>\n\n  <article class=\"event\" id=\"task-due-date-approaching\">\n    <header><h3>task.due_date_approaching</h3><span class=\"badge prod-only\">Production only</span></header>\n    <dl>\n      <dt>Description</dt><dd>Fired when a task's due date is approaching. The payload includes the granted <code>role</code>.</dd>\n      <dt>Trigger</dt><dd>A user is granted membership on a project.</dd>\n    </dl>\n    <pre>{\n  \"event\": \"member.added\",\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"user_id\": 93,\n  \"role\": \"member\",\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}</pre>\n    <p class=\"obs\">Observed in production: delivery <code>d-90005</code>, 2024-03-04T16:45:12Z, HTTP 200.</p>\n  </article>\n\n  <article class=\"event\" id=\"member-removed\">\n    <header><h3>member.removed</h3><span class=\"badge spec-prod\">Spec + Production</span></header>\n    <dl>\n      <dt>Description</dt><dd>Fired when a user's membership on a project is revoked.</dd>\n      <dt>Trigger</dt><dd>A user's membership is removed from a project.</dd>\n    </dl>\n    <pre>{\n  \"event\": \"member.removed\",\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"user_id\": 45,\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}</pre>\n    <p class=\"obs\">Observed in production: delivery <code>d-90009</code>, 2024-03-07T14:10:00Z, HTTP 200.</p>\n  </article>\n</section>\n\n<section id=\"subscribing\">\n  <h2>Subscribing to events</h2>\n  <p>\n    Register a webhook with <code>POST /webhooks</code>. The request requires a <code>url</code> and an\n    <code>events</code> array whose values must come from the ten spec-declared event names listed above.\n    An optional <code>secret</code> enables HMAC payload verification, and <code>active</code>\n    (default <code>true</code>) controls whether the subscription is live. Keep the secret out of\n    client-side code and rotate it by re-registering the webhook with a new <code>secret</code> value.\n  </p>\n</section>\n\n<section id=\"sources\">\n  <h2>Source reconciliation</h2>\n  <table class=\"sources\">\n    <thead>\n      <tr><th>Event</th><th>Declared in OpenAPI spec (subscribable)</th><th>Observed in production log</th><th>Sample delivery</th></tr>\n    </thead>\n    <tbody>\n      <tr><td><code>task.created</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90001</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>task.updated</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90002</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>task.deleted</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90010</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>task.assigned</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90006</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>task.commented</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90003</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>project.created</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90012</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>project.archived</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90004</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>project.deleted</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90008</code> (failed, 3 retries)</td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>member.added</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90005</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>member.removed</code></td><td>Yes</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90009</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>task.due_date_approaching</code></td><td>No</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90007</code></td></tr>\n      <tr><td><code>task.overdue</code></td><td>No</td><td>Yes</td><td><code>d-90011</code></td></tr>\n    </tbody>\n  </table>\n  <h3 id=\"gaps\">Known gaps</h3>\n  <ul>\n    <li><strong>Spec gap:</strong> <code>task.due_date_approaching</code> and <code>task.overdue</code> are emitted in production but absent from the <code>events</code> enum. 1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.
102: 
103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## DELETE /api/projects/:id
114: 
115: Delete a project. All tasks in the project will also be deleted.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Errors
120: 
121: Errors return JSON: `{"error": "message"}`.
122: 
123: Common codes: 400, 401, 404, 500.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Webhooks
128: 
129: POST /api/webhooks - register a webhook. Body: `url`, `events` (array).
130: 
131: GET /api/webhooks - list webhooks.
132: 
133: DELETE /api/webhooks/:id - remove a webhook.
134: 
135: Events: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `project.created`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## Notes
140: 
141: - Rate limit: 60 req/min.

# TaskFlow API Documentation

**Version**: 2.0
**Last Updated**: March 2024

Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.

## Authentication

All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
```

You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

---

## Tasks

### GET /api/v2/tasks

Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.

**Query Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |

\n\n
\n

TaskFlow API — Webhook Event Catalog

\n

\n This catalog lists every webhook event the TaskFlow platform emits, combining two sources:\n the events declared as subscribable values in the OpenAPI 3.0 specification\n (taskflow_openapi_v2_extract.yaml, API version 2.0.1) and the events actually observed\n in a production delivery log (webhook_delivery_log.json, export dated 2024-03-10).\n

\n

\n Sources reconciled: OpenAPI spec (declares 10 event values) ·\n Production delivery log for webhook 301 → https://integrations.acme.corp/taskflow/events\n (12 deliveries, 12 unique event types, 11 successful / 1 failed).\n

\n
\n\n
\n

At a glance

\n
\n
12
Total event types documented
\n
10
Declared in spec & observed in production
\n
2
Observed in production only (not in spec)
\n
1
Failed delivery in sample (3 retries)
\n
\n

\n Spec + Production — subscribable via the events array on\n POST /webhooks and confirmed firing in production.\n   Production only — observed firing in production but\n not declared in the specification's events enum; treat as undocumented until the\n spec is updated (see Known gaps).\n

\n
\n\n
\n

Event catalog

\n\n

Task events

\n\n
\n

task.created

Spec + Production
\n
\n
Description
Fired when a new task is created in a project.
\n
Trigger
Successful POST /tasks.
\n
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.created\",\n  \"task_id\": 1042,\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90001, 2024-03-01T14:22:00Z, HTTP 200.

\n
\n\n
\n

task.updated

Spec + Production
\n
\n
Description
Fired when one or more fields of an existing task change. The changed_fields array names the fields that were modified, so consumers can react selectively.
\n
Trigger
Successful PUT /tasks/{taskId}, or any other mutation that alters task fields (for example POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign).
\n
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.updated\",\n  \"task_id\": 1042,\n  \"changed_fields\": [\"status\", \"assignee_id\"],\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90002, 2024-03-01T15:05:33Z, HTTP 200.

\n
\n\n
\n

task.assigned

Spec + Production
\n
\n
Description
Fired when a task is assigned to a user. Note that in production, task updates that change the assignee also emitted task.updated — consumers should be prepared to receive both events for one assignment.
\n
Trigger
Successful POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign, or an update that sets assignee_id.
\n
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.assigned\",\n  \"task_id\": 1050,\n  \"assignee_id\": 93,\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90006, 2024-03-05T10:02:00Z, HTTP 200.

\n
\n\n
\n

task.commented

Spec + Production
\n
\n
Description
Fired when a comment is added to a task. The payload identifies the comment so consumers can fetch or display it.
\n
Trigger
A new comment is posted on the task.
\n
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.commented\",\n  \"task_id\": 1042,\n  \"comment_id\": 5567,\n  \"actor_id\": 82\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90003, 2024-03-02T09:17:44Z, HTTP 200.

\n
\n\n
\n

Spec + Production
\n
\n
Description
Fired when a task is deleted. Includes the owning project_id so consumers can clean up project-scoped state.
\n
Trigger
Successful DELETE /tasks/{taskId}, or deletion of a task via project cascade.
\n
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.deleted\",\n  \"task_id\": 999,\n  \"project_id\": 3,\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90010, 2024-03-08T09:00:00Z, HTTP 200.

Production only
\n
\n
Description
Fired when a task's due date is approaching. The payload carries the due date and the number of days remaining. Both scheduled events in the sample fired at exactly 00:00:00Z, consistent with a once-daily scheduled job.
\n
Trigger
Scheduled daily check; fired while the task's due date is still in the future within the reminder window (observed at days_remaining: 9).
\n
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.due_date_approaching\",\n  \"task_id\": 1042,\n  \"due_date\": \"2024-03-15T00:00:00Z\",\n  \"days_remaining\": 9\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90007, 2024-03-06T00:00:00Z, HTTP 200.

\n
\n\n
\n

task.overdue

Production only
\n
\n
Description
Fired when a task's due date has passed without the task being completed. The payload carries the due date and the number of days overdue. Like task.due_date_approaching, it fires from the daily scheduled run.
\n
Trigger
Scheduled daily check; fired once the due date has passed (observed at days_overdue: 1).
\n
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"task.overdue\",\n  \"task_id\": 1042,\n  \"due_date\": \"2024-03-15T00:00:00Z\",\n  \"days_overdue\": 1\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90011, 2024-03-16T00:00:00Z, HTTP 200.

project.deleted

Spec + Production
\n
\n
Description
Fired when a project is deleted. This is the only event in the sample log with a failed delivery: the first attempt returned HTTP 502 and was retried 3 times before being marked permanently failed. Consumers that must not miss this event (for example, to tear down synced resources) should implement a reconciliation check.
\n
Trigger
Successful DELETE /projects/{projectId}.
\n
\n 
{\n  \"event\": \"project.deleted\",\n  \"project_id\": 3,\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90008, 2024-03-07T08:20:00Z, HTTP 502, retry_attempts: 3, final_status: \"failed\".

\n

Description
Fired when a user's membership on a project is revoked.
\n
Trigger
A user's membership is removed from a project.

{\n  \"event\": \"member.removed\",\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"user_id\": 45,\n  \"actor_id\": 57\n}
\n

Observed in production: delivery d-90009, 2024-03-07T14:10:00Z, HTTP 200.

\n
\n
\n\n
\n

Subscribing to events

\n

\n Register a webhook with POST /webhooks. The request requires a url and an\n events array whose values must come from the ten spec-declared event names listed above.\n An optional secret enables HMAC payload verification, and active\n (default true) controls whether the subscription is live. A successful registration\n returns 201 Created. Delete a subscription with DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId},\n which returns 204 No Content.\n

\n
\n Undocumented events cannot be subscribed to. task.due_date_approaching and\n task.overdue are emitted by the platform but are not part of the events enum in the\n specification, so they cannot be requested at registration time. Existing endpoints observed receiving them\n (such as webhook 301 in the sample) appear to receive all events regardless of subscription.\n If your integration depends on these events, verify actual delivery behavior against your own endpoint and\n track the spec update in the discrepancy report before relying on them.\n
\n
\n\n
\n

Delivery and retry semantics

\n

\n TaskFlow delivers events by HTTP POST to the destination URL registered for the webhook.\n A delivery is considered successful when the endpoint responds with an HTTP 2xx status.\n When the endpoint returns an error response, TaskFlow retries the delivery — the production sample shows\n 3 retry attempts for the failed project.deleted delivery\n (d-90008, destination returned 502) — and if all attempts fail, the delivery is\n marked final_status: \"failed\" and is not re-attempted further.\n

\n

Recommendations for consumer endpoints:

\n
    \n
  • Respond quickly with 2xx and process the payload asynchronously; slow handlers risk timeouts.
    • \n
  • Treat event delivery as at-least-once: deduplicate using task_id/project_id plus the event type and timestamp.
    • \n
  • Do not rely on ordering between events; in the sample, related events (task.updated and task.assigned) can both fire for one user action.
    • \n
  • Monitor for missed project.deleted-style events by periodically reconciling state, since permanently failed deliveries are not re-sent.
    • \n
\n
\n\n
\n

Verifying payloads (HMAC)

\n

\n When a webhook is registered with a secret, TaskFlow signs each payload with that shared secret\n using HMAC. Verify the signature server-side before trusting the payload contents. Keep the secret out of\n client-side code and rotate it by re-registering the webhook with a new secret value.\n

\n
\n\n
\n

Known gaps

\n
    \n
  • Spec gap: task.due_date_approaching and task.overdue are emitted in production but absent from the events enum. File them for addition to the specification.
    • \n
  • Docs gap: the legacy v1 documentation advertised only 4 events (task.created, task.updated, task.deleted, project.created). The current catalog supersedes that list entirely.

# TaskFlow API Documentation

**Version**: 2.0
**Last Updated**: March 2024

Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.

## Authentication

All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
```

You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

---

### GET /api/v2/tasks

Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.

**Query Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |

[{"content": "## Goal

Act as a senior technical writer for "TaskFlow" (a SaaS project management platform) and produce **five publication-ready deliverables** in `/work/output/`, reconciling inconsistent source materials:

1. **Discrepancy report (CSV)** — cross-referencing the OpenAPI 3.0 YAML spec against current Markdown docs, incorporating signals from the audit tracker beyond simple diff.
2. **API documentation style guide (Markdown, ≥1500 words)** — governing all future TaskFlow API docs, grounded in local references + GitLab's REST API documentation guidelines (pinned snapshot; no internet).
3. **Complete rewritten TaskFlow API v2 docs (Markdown)** — every endpoint conforming to the style guide, incorporating everything the spec knows that docs don't, resolving every audit-tracker issue.
4. **Webhook event catalog (HTML)** — synthesizing spec-declared events with production-log-observed events; each entry documents event name, description, trigger condition, example payload, and provenance across both sources.
5. **v1-to-v2 migration guide (Markdown)** — developer-facing, using legacy v1 docs + reconciled v2 materials.

## Instructions

- **Source files** (in `/work/task_folder/`): `TASK_INSTRUCTIONS.txt`, `doc_audit_tracker.csv` (18 endpoint audit rows with priority/status/notes), `restapidocs_combined_template.md` (RESTAPIDocs template), `taskflow_api_docs_current.md` (v2 docs), `taskflow_api_docs_current_v1.md`, `taskflow_openapi_v2_extract.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.0.3, version 2.0.1), `webhook_delivery_log.json`. External reference: `/work/task_folder/references/gitlab_api_doc_styleguide.md` (pinned GitLab style guide snapshot; internet unavailable).
- **Write all deliverables to `/work/output/`.**
- Audit tracker contains signal beyond diff comparison (terminology drift, missing auth info, description quality) — must be captured in the CSV and resolved in the rewrite.
- Style guide grounded in conventions of the local references (GitLab verb tables, cURL conventions, attribute tables; RESTAPIDocs URL/Method/Auth/Permissions format).

## Discoveries

**Key spec-vs-docs discrepancies found (45 recorded, D-001 to D-045):**
- **8 operations entirely missing from current v2 docs** (exist in spec): `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /projects/{projectId}`, `POST /webhooks`, `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}`, `GET /search/tasks`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`.
- Schema deltas: status enum missing `blocked`; priority missing `urgent`; sort missing `due_date`; role missing `viewer`; `label`, `include`, `fields`, `watchers`, `template_id`, `visibility`, `cascade`, `notify` params undocumented; `title` maxLength 255 (docs) vs 200 (spec); `per_page` default 20/max 100 (docs) vs 25/200 (spec).
- Direct contradiction: docs claim projects endpoint has **no pagination**; spec defines `page`/`per_page` for it (spec wins per resolution).
- Path params: docs use `{id}`, spec uses `{taskId}`/`{projectId}`/`{webhookId}`.
- Global: version 2.0 vs 2.0.1; docs say "all API calls require API key" but spec has open endpoint `/auth/login`; two conflicting error formats (structured envelope is canonical, flat shape legacy); Unix timestamps (`projects.created`, `users.last_login`) inconsistent with ISO 8601.
- **Webhook events**: spec declares 10 events; production log shows 12 unique — all 10 spec events observed, plus 2 observed-only (`task.due_date_approaching`, `task.overdue`) not declared in spec. Catalog must have 12 entries with provenance badges.
- **Retry evidence**: delivery `d-90008` (`project.deleted`) returned 502 with `retry_attempts: 3`, `final_status: failed` → documented retry policy (3 attempts, backoff, then marked failed).
- v1→v2 migration deltas: `X-API-Key` header → Bearer token; assign endpoint `PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign` → `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign` with `user_id` → `assignee_id`; v1 `/api/tasks/:id/comments` and `/api/tasks/:id/history` endpoints folded into `?include=` expansion; `/api/search` → `/api/v2/search/tasks` (cross-entity `type` param removed); field renames `desc`→`description`, `deadline`(Unix)→`due_date`(ISO 8601), `assigned_to`→`assignee_id`, `project`→`project_id`, `org`→`organization_id`; pagination `limit`/`offset` → `page`/`per_page` with `meta`; error format `{"error":"message"}` → structured envelope; webhook events 4 → 10 declared (+2 observed); rate limit 60/min → 100 (free)/1000 (paid).

**Environment constraint:** Writing to `/tmp` is blocked by an `external_directory` deny rule. Created `/work/.tmp_build/gen_discrepancy_csv.py` as a Python generator (needed because hand-written CSV had comma-in-value quoting bugs). **Cleanup of `/work/.tmp_build/` still pending.**

## Accomplished

- ✅ **`/work/output/discrepancy_report.csv`** — complete; regenerated via Python csv writer; validated (46 rows incl. header, all exactly 10 fields). Columns: discrepancy_id, endpoint, http_method, category, summary, openapi_spec_value, markdown_docs_value, audit_tracker_signal, severity, recommended_resolution.
- ✅ **`/work/output/taskflow_api_style_guide.md`** — complete; 2178 words (exceeds 1500 minimum). Covers source-of-truth hierarchy (spec > docs > audit tracker > production evidence), page structure, GitLab-style verb tables, attribute table rules, cURL/JSON example conventions, error/status codes, cross-cutting conventions (auth, pagination, rate limiting, ISO 8601 timestamps, webhooks), terminology table, deprecation handling, review checklist mapped to audit tracker columns.
- ✅ **`/work/output/taskflow_api_v2_docs.md`** — just written. Full rewrite covering all 16 operations: auth (login w/ mfa_code + 403 MFA, refresh), tasks (list w/ label/blocked/25/200/due_date, create w/ watchers/urgent/maxLength 200, retrieve w/ include, update w/ 409 + response example, delete w/ permissions, assign w/ notify + reassignment semantics), projects (list w/ pagination + viewer, create w/ template_id/visibility, retrieve/update/delete w/ cascade), users/me w/ fields param, search/tasks, webhooks (create w/ 10 events + HMAC secret + retry policy notes, delete). Uses YAML front matter, metadata blocks (URL/Method/Auth/Permissions), request/response attribute tables, cURL examples with long options, error tables, Notes sections.
- ⏳ **`/work/output/webhook_event_catalog.html`** — **NOT yet written**. Planned: standalone HTML page with inline CSS, 12 event entries (10 spec-declared + production-observed; 2 production-only: `task.due_date_approaching`, `task.overdue`), each with name, description, trigger condition, example payload (JSON from delivery log `payload_excerpt`, fleshed out), provenance badges ("Declared in spec + Observed in production" vs "Production only — undeclared in spec"), plus summary/legend and retry/delivery semantics note referencing d-90008.
- ⏳ **`/work/output/v1_to_v2_migration_guide.md`** — **NOT yet written**. Planned content: base URL change, auth migration (X-API-Key → Bearer + login/refresh flow), endpoint mapping table, breaking changes (PUT→POST assign, pagination scheme, timestamps, field renames, error format, comments/history → include, search move, webhook event expansion), before/after cURL examples, deprecation window, checklist.
- ⏳ **Final validation** — remaining: word counts, CSV re-parse, HTML sanity check; **cleanup of `/work/.tmp_build/`**.

1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.
102: 
103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## DELETE /api/projects/:id
114: 
115: Delete a project. All tasks in the project will also be deleted.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Errors
120: 
121: Errors return JSON: `{"error": "message"}`.
122: 
123: Common codes: 400, 401, 404, 500.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Webhooks
128: 
129: POST /api/webhooks - register a webhook. Body: `url`, `events` (array).
130: 
131: GET /api/webhooks - list webhooks.
132: 
133: DELETE /api/webhooks/:id - remove a webhook.
134: 
135: Events: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `project.created`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## Notes
140: 
141: - Rate limit: 60 req/min.
142: - All timestamps are Unix.
143: - Contact support@taskflow.io for help.

(End of file - total 143 lines)

- 100 requests per minute for free tier
- 1000 requests per minute for paid plans

# TaskFlow API Documentation

**Version**: 2.0
**Last Updated**: March 2024

Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.

## Authentication

All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
```

You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

---

## Tasks

### GET /api/v2/tasks

Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.

**Query Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |

1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.

103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).

**Version**: 2.0
**Last Updated**: March 2024

Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.

## Authentication

All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
```

You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

| status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |

reasoning_content:
Base URL: v1 `https://api.taskflow.io/api`, v2 `https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2`. Good.

Now write both deliverables. First the HTML webhook catalog.

Design: clean standalone HTML with inline CSS. Sections:
1. Header: title, generated date, sources
2. Summary cards: total events (12), declared in spec (10), production-only (2), spec-declared but still observed? All 10 observed. Failed delivery example.
3. Legend for provenance badges
4. Event catalog: 12 cards or a table. A table might be cleaner for scanning, but cards give room for payloads. I'll do cards grouped: Task events, Project events, Membership events, plus the two production-only ones in their natural groups but with "Production only" badge.
5. Delivery & retry semantics section (grounded in d-90008)
6. Security (HMAC secret from spec)
7. Subscription (POST /webhooks with events array; 10 subscribable events; note the 2 production-only events are not selectable in the enum)
8. Footer note about payload excerpts being reconstructed from delivery-log excerpts.

Keep it professional and complete. Let me write it.

Then the migration guide. Structure:
- YAML front matter (title, description)
- Overview
- Who needs to migrate / timeline (deprecation window — v1 docs don't give a sunset date; I should say "contact TaskFlow support for your tenant's v1 retirement date" rather than fabricate. The style guide I wrote has deprecation handling principles. I'll state no EOL date was published in source materials and advise planning accordingly — honest.)
- Quick summary table of breaking changes
- Base URL
- Authentication (X-API-Key → Bearer; new login/refresh endpoints; note current v2 docs say API key via Bearer while spec has /auth/login with JWT — from my earlier analysis: spec has POST /auth/login (with mfa_code, 403 MFA) and POST /auth/refresh. The v2 docs describe static API keys. This is itself a discrepancy (D-0xx). For the migration guide, I should cover both: v1 static key → v2 Bearer; and mention token-based auth via /auth/login exists per spec. I'll present: Authorization: Bearer <token_or_api_key>, and describe the login/refresh flow as available for user-token-based integrations.)
- Field renames table (desc→description, deadline→due_date + Unix→ISO 8601, assigned_to→assignee_id, project→project_id, org→organization_id, user_id→assignee_id on assign)
- Endpoint mapping table (v1 → v2):
  - GET /api/tasks → GET /api/v2/tasks (params: status, project→project_id, limit/offset→page/per_page; sort now available)
  - POST /api/tasks → POST /api/v2/tasks (body renames; deadline Unix → due_date ISO; priority urgent added; watchers added)
  - GET /api/tasks/:id → GET /tasks/{taskId} (+ include for comments/history)
  - PUT /api/tasks/:id → PATCH? Wait — what does the v2 spec use for updating a task? From my earlier summary: "update w/ 409 + response example" — I need to check whether v2 task update is PUT or PATCH. Let me check the spec paths quickly before writing. I remember the rewrite covered update with 409 conflict. The method — I believe spec has put on /tasks/{taskId}. Let me verify.
  - DELETE /api/tasks/:id → DELETE /tasks/{taskId}
  - PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign → POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign (user_id → assignee_id; response includes notify param)
  - GET /api/tasks/:id/comments → GET /tasks/{taskId}?include=comments
  - POST /api/tasks/:id/comments → REMOVED? Hmm. In v2, how do you add comments? My earlier analysis said comments/history endpoints folded into include param for reading. Posting a comment — I don't recall a POST comments endpoint in the spec. I need to check the spec's full path list to be accurate. Let me look at the spec paths.
  - GET /api/tasks/:id/history → GET /tasks/{taskId}?include=history
  - GET /api/projects → GET /projects (now paginated page/per_page + meta)
  - POST /api/projects → POST /projects (desc→description; template_id, visibility added)
  - DELETE /api/projects/:id → DELETE /projects/{projectId} (cascade param; default behavior? cascade: false default? Spec: query param cascade "If true, deletes all tasks within the project." So v1 "all tasks also deleted" → v2 requires cascade=true for that; otherwise project with tasks may fail or orphans. I documented this in v2 docs; I'll check what I wrote. For migration guide: warn that deleting a project no longer implicitly deletes tasks unless cascade=true.)
  - GET /api/users/current → GET /users/me (org→organization_id; fields param; created timestamps ISO except users.last_login Unix)
  - GET /api/search → GET /search/tasks (type param removed; project_id filter; cross-entity search gone)
  - POST /api/webhooks → POST /webhooks (url, events[], secret, active; 201; 10 events)
  - GET /api/webhooks → hmm, is there a GET /webhooks in the v2 spec? My earlier analysis: "8 operations entirely missing from current v2 docs (exist in spec): POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign, GET/PUT/DELETE /projects/{projectId}, POST /webhooks, DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}, GET /search/tasks, POST /auth/login, POST /auth/refresh." No GET /webhooks listed — so v2 spec has no list-webhooks operation. Migration note: GET /api/webhooks has no v2 equivalent in the spec (removed/unspecified) — flag it.
  - DELETE /api/webhooks/:id → DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId} (204)
  - GET /api/projects/:id and PUT /api/projects/:id — v1 doc doesn't document these! v1 doc only has GET /api/projects, POST /api/projects, DELETE /api/projects/:id. So retrieve/update project are new in v2 docs (they exist in spec). I can mention them as "new capabilities".
- Error format change ({"error": "message"} → structured envelope {"error": {"code", "message", ...}}; legacy flat shape still on some endpoints)
- Pagination change (limit/offset → page/per_page + meta; per_page default 25 max 200 per spec)
- Timestamps (Unix → ISO 8601; exceptions projects.created, users.last_login remain Unix — documented as known inconsistency per discrepancy report)
- Rate limits (60/min → 100 free / 1000 paid; 429 + X-RateLimit-Remaining)
- Webhooks (4 events → 10 declared + 2 observed undocumented: task.due_date_approaching, task.overdue; HMAC secret now supported)
- Status/priority enum expansions (status + blocked/archived; priority + urgent) — additive, low risk
- Validation tightening: title maxLength 200 (was 255 in v2 docs, but v1 didn't specify; spec says 200 — for migration guide, say max 200 per spec), 409 conflict on stale update (If-Match? need to check), 422 validation errors
- Deleted/changed behaviors: assign PUT→POST, search type param removed
- Before/after cURL examples: list tasks, create task, assign, comments→include, search, webhook create, error handling
- Migration checklist
- Known issues/gotchas section referencing the discrepancy report (projects pagination contradiction resolved to spec; error format standardization in progress; Unix timestamps in two fields)

Before writing, I must verify: (1) does the spec use PUT or PATCH for task update? (2) full spec path list. (3) What I wrote in my v2 docs for the delete-project cascade default and 409 conditions so the migration guide matches my own rewrite. Let me read the spec paths overview and my v2 docs' relevant bits.

[{"content": "## Goal

Act as a senior technical writer for "TaskFlow" (a SaaS project management platform) and produce **five publication-ready deliverables** in `/work/output/`, reconciling inconsistent source materials:

1. **Discrepancy report (CSV)** — cross-referencing the OpenAPI 3.0 YAML spec against current Markdown docs, incorporating signals from the audit tracker beyond simple diff.
2. **API documentation style guide (Markdown, ≥1500 words)** — governing all future TaskFlow API docs, grounded in local references + GitLab's REST API documentation guidelines (pinned snapshot; no internet).
3. **Complete rewritten TaskFlow API v2 docs (Markdown)** — every endpoint conforming to the style guide, incorporating everything the spec knows that docs don't, resolving every audit-tracker issue.
4. **Webhook event catalog (HTML)** — synthesizing spec-declared events with production-log-observed events; each entry documents event name, description, trigger condition, example payload, and provenance across both sources.
5. **v1-to-v2 migration guide (Markdown)** — developer-facing, using legacy v1 docs + reconciled v2 materials.

## Instructions

- **Source files** (in `/work/task_folder/`): `TASK_INSTRUCTIONS.txt`, `doc_audit_tracker.csv` (18 endpoint audit rows with priority/status/notes), `restapidocs_combined_template.md` (RESTAPIDocs template), `taskflow_api_docs_current.md` (v2 docs), `taskflow_api_docs_current_v1.md`, `taskflow_openapi_v2_extract.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.0.3, version 2.0.1), `webhook_delivery_log.json`. External reference: `/work/task_folder/references/gitlab_api_doc_styleguide.md` (pinned GitLab style guide snapshot; internet unavailable).
- **Write all deliverables to `/work/output/`.**
- Audit tracker contains signal beyond diff comparison (terminology drift, missing auth info, description quality) — must be captured in the CSV and resolved in the rewrite.
- Style guide grounded in conventions of the local references (GitLab verb tables, cURL conventions, attribute tables; RESTAPIDocs URL/Method/Auth/Permissions format).

## Discoveries

**Key spec-vs-docs discrepancies found (45 recorded, D-001 to D-045):**
- **8 operations entirely missing from current v2 docs** (exist in spec): `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /projects/{projectId}`, `POST /webhooks`, `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}`, `GET /search/tasks`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`.
- Schema deltas: status enum missing `blocked`; priority missing `urgent`; sort missing `due_date`; role missing `viewer`; `label`, `include`, `fields`, `watchers`, `template_id`, `visibility`, `cascade`, `notify` params undocumented; `title` maxLength 255 (docs) vs 200 (spec); `per_page` default 20/max 100 (docs) vs 25/200 (spec).
- Direct contradiction: docs claim projects endpoint has **no pagination**; spec defines `page`/`per_page` for it (spec wins per resolution).
- Path params: docs use `{id}`, spec uses `{taskId}`/`{projectId}`/`{webhookId}`.
- Global: version 2.0 vs 2.0.1; docs say "all API calls require API key" but spec has open endpoint `/auth/login`; two conflicting error formats (structured envelope is canonical, flat shape legacy); Unix timestamps (`projects.created`, `users.last_login`) inconsistent with ISO 8601.
- **Webhook events**: spec declares 10 events; production log shows 12 unique — all 10 spec events observed, plus 2 observed-only (`task.due_date_approaching`, `task.overdue`) not declared in spec. Catalog must have 12 entries with provenance badges.
- **Retry evidence**: delivery `d-90008` (`project.deleted`) returned 502 with `retry_attempts: 3`, `final_status: failed` → documented retry policy (3 attempts, backoff, then marked failed).
- v1→v2 migration deltas: `X-API-Key` header → Bearer token; assign endpoint `PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign` → `POST /tasks/{taskId}/assign` with `user_id` → `assignee_id`; v1 `/api/tasks/:id/comments` and `/api/tasks/:id/history` endpoints folded into `?include=` expansion; `/api/search` → `/api/v2/search/tasks` (cross-entity `type` param removed); field renames `desc`→`description`, `deadline`(Unix)→`due_date`(ISO 8601), `assigned_to`→`assignee_id`, `project`→`project_id`, `org`→`organization_id`; pagination `limit`/`offset` → `page`/`per_page` with `meta`; error format `{"error":"message"}` → structured envelope; webhook events 4 → 10 declared (+2 observed); rate limit 60/min → 100 (free)/1000 (paid).

**Environment constraint:** Writing to `/tmp` is blocked by an `external_directory` deny rule. Created `/work/.tmp_build/gen_discrepancy_csv.py` as a Python generator (needed because hand-written CSV had comma-in-value quoting bugs). **Cleanup of `/work/.tmp_build/` still pending.**

## Accomplished

- ✅ **`/work/output/discrepancy_report.csv`** — complete; regenerated via Python csv writer; validated (46 rows incl. header, all exactly 10 fields). Columns: discrepancy_id, endpoint, http_method, category, summary, openapi_spec_value, markdown_docs_value, audit_tracker_signal, severity, recommended_resolution.
- ✅ **`/work/output/taskflow_api_style_guide.md`** — complete; 2178 words (exceeds 1500 minimum). Covers source-of-truth hierarchy (spec > docs > audit tracker > production evidence), page structure, GitLab-style verb tables, attribute table rules, cURL/JSON example conventions, error/status codes, cross-cutting conventions (auth, pagination, rate limiting, ISO 8601 timestamps, webhooks), terminology table, deprecation handling, review checklist mapped to audit tracker columns.
- ✅ **`/work/output/taskflow_api_v2_docs.md`** — just written. Full rewrite covering all 16 operations: auth (login w/ mfa_code + 403 MFA, refresh), tasks (list w/ label/blocked/25/200/due_date, create w/ watchers/urgent/maxLength 200, retrieve w/ include, update w/ 409 + response example, delete w/ permissions, assign w/ notify + reassignment semantics), projects (list w/ pagination + viewer, create w/ template_id/visibility, retrieve/update/delete w/ cascade), users/me w/ fields param, search/tasks, webhooks (create w/ 10 events + HMAC secret + retry policy notes, delete). Uses YAML front matter, metadata blocks (URL/Method/Auth/Permissions), request/response attribute tables, cURL examples with long options, error tables, Notes sections.
- ⏳ **`/work/output/webhook_event_catalog.html`** — **NOT yet written**. Planned: standalone HTML page with inline CSS, 12 event entries (10 spec-declared + production-observed; 2 production-only: `task.due_date_approaching`, `task.overdue`), each with name, description, trigger condition, example payload (JSON from delivery log `payload_excerpt`, fleshed out), provenance badges ("Declared in spec + Observed in production" vs "Production only — undeclared in spec"), plus summary/legend and retry/delivery semantics note referencing d-90008.
- ⏳ **`/work/output/v1_to_v2_migration_guide.md`** — **NOT yet written**. Planned content: base URL change, auth migration (X-API-Key → Bearer + login/refresh flow), endpoint mapping table, breaking changes (PUT→POST assign, pagination scheme, timestamps, field renames, error format, comments/history → include, search move, webhook event expansion), before/after cURL examples, deprecation window, checklist.

1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.
102: 
103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## DELETE /api/projects/:id
114: 
115: Delete a project. All tasks in the project will also be deleted.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Errors
120: 
121: Errors return JSON: `{"error": "message"}`.
122: 
123: Common codes: 400, 401, 404, 500.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Webhooks
128: 
129: POST /api/webhooks - register a webhook. Body: `url`, `events` (array).
130: 
131: GET /api/webhooks - list webhooks.
132: 
133: DELETE /api/webhooks/:id - remove a webhook.
134: 
135: Events: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `project.created`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## Notes
140: 
141: - Rate limit: 60 req/min.
142: - All timestamps are Unix.
143: - Contact support@taskflow.io for help.

(End of file - total 143 lines)

# TaskFlow API Documentation

**Version**: 2.0
**Last Updated**: March 2024

Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.

## Authentication

All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
```

You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

---

## Tasks

### GET /api/v2/tasks

Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.

**Query Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |

3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`

5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
