201 characters returns `422`; an unknown `assignee_id` returns `422`; `due_date` values without a UTC offset are interpreted as UTC.\n\n---\n\n### Retrieve a task\n\nRetrieves a single task by ID. Pass the task ID as the `taskId` path parameter. Optionally expand related resources with the `include` query parameter.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/tasks/{taskId}`\n\n**Method**: `GET`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Read access to the project containing the task\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute | Type    | Required | Description                                                                     |\n|-----------|---------|----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `taskId`  | integer | Yes      | The ID of the task to retrieve.                                                   |\n| `include` | string  | No       | Comma-separated list of related resources to expand. One or more of `comments`, `history`, `attachments`. |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042?include=comments,history\"\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `200 OK`\n\nReturns the task object with the same attributes as the task objects in [List all tasks](#list-all-tasks). When `include` is supplied, each requested collection is added as a top-level key (`comments`, `history`, `attachments`).\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 1042,\n  \"title\": \"Fix login bug\",\n  \"description\": \"Users are unable to login with SSO\",\n  \"status\": \"open\",\n  \"priority\": \"high\",\n  \"assignee_id\": 57,\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-03-01T14:22:00Z\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2024-03-01T14:22:00Z\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2024-03-15T00:00:00Z\",\n  \"comments\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": 5567,\n      \"author_id\": 82,\n      \"body\": \"Reproduced on staging.\",\n      \"created_at\": \"2024-03-02T09:17:00Z\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                            |\n|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                              |\n| 404         | Task not found, or you do not have access to it.    |\n\n---\n\n### Update a task\n\nUpdates a task. Partial updates are supported: send only the fields you want to change. Fields not included in the request body remain unchanged.\n\n```plaintext\nPUT /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/tasks/{taskId}`\n\n**Method**: `PUT`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Write access to the project containing the task\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute     | Type          | Required | Description                                                       |\n|---------------|---------------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `taskId`      | integer       | Yes      | The ID of the task to update.                                      |\n| `assignee_id` | integer       | No       | Assigned user ID. Set to `null` to unassign.                       |\n| `description` | string        | No       | Task description.                                                  |\n| `due_date`    | string        | No       | Due date in ISO 8601 format, or `null` to clear.                   |\n| `priority`    | string        | No       | One of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`, `urgent`.               |\n| `project_id`  | integer       | No       | Project to move the task to.                                       |\n| `status`      | string        | No       | Must be a valid status string.                                     |\n| `tags`        | string array  | No       | Replaces the tag list.                                             |\n| `title`       | string        | No       | Task title. Maximum 200 characters.                                |\n| `watchers`    | integer array | No       | Replaces the watcher list.                                         |\n\nThe `id` and `created_at` fields cannot be modified.\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --request PUT \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042\" \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\n    \"status\": \"in_progress\",\n    \"assignee_id\": 57\n  }'\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `200 OK`\n\nReturns the updated task object:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 1042,\n  \"title\": \"Fix login bug\",\n  \"description\": \"Users are unable to login with SSO\",\n  \"status\": \"in_progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"high\",\n  \"assignee_id\": 57,\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-03-01T14:22:00Z\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2024-03-05T09:41:12Z\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2024-03-15T00:00:00Z\"\n}\n```\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                          |\n|-------------|---------------------------------------------------|\n| 400         | Bad request - malformed body or invalid values.   |\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                            |\n| 403         | You do not have write access to this task.        |\n| 404         | Task not found.                                   |\n| 409         | Conflict - concurrent modification detected. Re-fetch the task and retry. |\n\n---\n\n### Delete a task\n\nDeletes a task permanently. This action cannot be undone.\n\n```plaintext\nDELETE /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/tasks/{taskId}`\n\n**Method**: `DELETE`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Admin or owner on the project containing the task. Regular members can delete only tasks they created.\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute | Type    | Required | Description                  |\n|-----------|---------|----------|-------------------------------|\n| `taskId`  | integer | Yes      | The ID of the task to delete. |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --request DELETE \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042\"\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `204 No Content`\n\nThe response body is empty.\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                                     |\n|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                                       |\n| 403         | Forbidden - insufficient permissions.                        |\n| 404         | Task not found.                                              |\n\n---\n\n### Assign a task\n\nAssigns a task to a user. Assigning a new assignee replaces any existing assignment. By default the assignee receives a notification; set `notify` to `false` to suppress it. This endpoint also works as an unassignment helper: pass `assignee_id: null` with `notify` to control notification behavior on unassignment.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/tasks/{taskId}/assign\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/tasks/{taskId}/assign`\n\n**Method**: `POST`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Write access to the project containing the task\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute     | Type    | Required | Description                                          |\n|---------------|---------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------|\n| `taskId`      | integer | Yes      | The ID of the task to assign.                         |\n| `assignee_id` | integer | Yes      | The user ID of the assignee.                          |\n| `notify`      | boolean | No       | Whether to send a notification to the assignee. Default is `true`. |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --request POST \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1050/assign\" \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\n    \"assignee_id\": 93,\n    \"notify\": true\n  }'\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `200 OK`\n\nReturns the updated task object:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 1050,\n  \"title\": \"Prepare Q2 report\",\n  \"status\": \"open\",\n  \"priority\": \"medium\",\n  \"assignee_id\": 93,\n  \"project_id\": 12,\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-03-04T09:00:00Z\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2024-03-05T10:02:00Z\",\n  \"due_date\": null\n}\n```\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                                     |\n|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|\n| 400         | Bad request - `assignee_id` missing or malformed.            |\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                                       |\n| 404         | Task or user not found. An invalid assignee is reported here. |\n\n---\n\n## Projects\n\nUse this API to create, retrieve, update, and delete projects.\n\n### List all projects\n\nLists all projects the authenticated user has access to. Results are paginated; pass `page` and `per_page` to control paging. Projects are returned in alphabetical order by name.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/projects\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/projects`\n\n**Method**: `GET`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: None (results are scoped to your organization and memberships)\n\n**Query parameters**\n\n| Attribute  | Type    | Required | Description                                                        |\n|------------|---------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `archived` | boolean | No       | If `true`, include archived projects. Default is `false`.           |\n| `page`     | integer | No       | Page number. Default is `1`.                                        |\n| `per_page` | integer | No       | Results per page. Default is `25`. Maximum is `200`.                |\n| `role`     | string  | No       | Filter by your role in the project. One of `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `viewer`. |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects?role=owner&page=1\"\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `200 OK`\n\n| Attribute               | Type         | Description                                          |\n|-------------------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------|\n| `data[]`                | object array | Project objects.                                       |\n| `data[].id`             | integer      | Project ID.                                            |\n| `data[].name`           | string       | Project name.                                          |\n| `data[].description`    | string       | Project description, or `null`.                        |\n| `data[].owner_id`       | integer      | User ID of the project owner.                          |\n| `data[].created`        | integer      | Legacy Unix timestamp. Migrates to ISO 8601 `created_at` in API v3. |\n| `data[].member_count`   | integer      | Number of project members.                             |\n| `data[].task_count`     | integer      | Number of tasks in the project.                        |\n| `data[].archived`       | boolean      | Whether the project is archived.                       |\n| `meta.current_page`     | integer      | Current page number.                                   |\n| `meta.total_pages`      | integer      | Total number of pages.                                 |\n| `meta.total_count`      | integer      | Total number of matching projects.                     |\n\n```json\n{\n  \"data\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": 12,\n      \"name\": \"Website Redesign\",\n      \"description\": \"Q2 2024 website overhaul\",\n      \"owner_id\": 57,\n      \"created\": 1709312400,\n      \"member_count\": 8,\n      \"task_count\": 45,\n      \"archived\": false\n    }\n  ],\n  \"meta\": {\n    \"current_page\": 1,\n    \"total_pages\": 1,\n    \"total_count\": 3\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Notes**\n\n- This endpoint previously returned a bare `projects` array with no pagination. It now follows the standard `data` + `meta` list envelope. If you parsed the bare array, update your client.\n- `created` is a legacy Unix timestamp; see [Timestamps](#timestamps).\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                    |\n|-------------|---------------------------------------------|\n| 400         | Bad request - invalid filter value.         |\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                      |\n\n---\n\n### Create a project\n\nCreates a new project. The `name` is required and must be unique within your organization.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/projects\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/projects`\n\n**Method**: `POST`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: None (the creating user becomes the owner)\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute     | Type    | Required | Description                                                            |\n|---------------|---------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `name`        | string  | Yes      | Project name. Maximum 100 characters. Unique within the organization.   |\n| `description` | string  | No       | Optional project description.                                           |\n| `template_id` | integer | No       | Create the project from an existing project template.                   |\n| `visibility`  | string  | No       | One of `private`, `internal`, `public`. Default is `private`.           |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --request POST \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects\" \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\n    \"name\": \"My New Project\",\n    \"description\": \"Optional project description\",\n    \"visibility\": \"internal\"\n  }'\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `201 Created`\n\n| Attribute     | Type    | Description                            |\n|---------------|---------|-----------------------------------------|\n| `id`          | integer | Auto-generated project ID.              |\n| `name`        | string  | The project name.                       |\n| `description` | string  | Project description, or `null`.         |\n| `owner_id`    | integer | ID of the creating user.                |\n| `created`     | integer | Legacy Unix timestamp.                  |\n| `member_count`| integer | Always `1` for new projects.            |\n| `task_count`  | integer | Always `0` for new projects.            |\n| `archived`    | boolean | Always `false` for new projects.        |\n| `visibility`  | string  | The project visibility setting.         |\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 16,\n  \"name\": \"My New Project\",\n  \"description\": \"Optional project description\",\n  \"owner_id\": 57,\n  \"created\": 1709654400,\n  \"member_count\": 1,\n  \"task_count\": 0,\n  \"archived\": false,\n  \"visibility\": \"internal\"\n}\n```\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                                     |\n|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|\n| 400         | Bad request - malformed body.                                 |\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                                        |\n| 422         | Validation error - name missing, too long, or not unique.     |\n\n---\n\n### Retrieve a project\n\nRetrieves a single project by ID.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/projects/{projectId}`\n\n**Method**: `GET`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Read access to the project\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute   | Type    | Required | Description                     |\n|-------------|---------|----------|----------------------------------|\n| `projectId` | integer | Yes      | The ID of the project to retrieve. |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/12\"\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `200 OK`\n\nReturns a project object with the same attributes as the project objects in [List all projects](#list-all-projects), plus `visibility`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 12,\n  \"name\": \"Website Redesign\",\n  \"description\": \"Q2 2024 website overhaul\",\n  \"owner_id\": 57,\n  \"created\": 1709312400,\n  \"member_count\": 8,\n  \"task_count\": 45,\n  \"archived\": false,\n  \"visibility\": \"internal\"\n}\n```\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                         |\n|-------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                           |\n| 404         | Project not found, or you do not have access to it. |\n\n---\n\n### Update a project\n\nUpdates a project. Partial updates are supported: send only the fields you want to change.\n\n```plaintext\nPUT /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/projects/{projectId}`\n\n**Method**: `PUT`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Admin or owner on the project\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute     | Type    | Required | Description                                              |\n|---------------|---------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------|\n| `projectId`   | integer | Yes      | The ID of the project to update.                           |\n| `archived`    | boolean | No       | Set to `true` to archive the project, `false` to restore.  |\n| `description` | string  | No       | Project description.                                       |\n| `name`        | string  | No       | Project name. Maximum 100 characters.                      |\n| `visibility`  | string  | No       | One of `private`, `internal`, `public`.                    |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --request PUT \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/12\" \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\n    \"name\": \"Website Redesign - Phase 2\",\n    \"archived\": false\n  }'\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `200 OK`\n\nReturns the updated project object:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 12,\n  \"name\": \"Website Redesign - Phase 2\",\n  \"description\": \"Q2 2024 website overhaul\",\n  \"owner_id\": 57,\n  \"created\": 1709312400,\n  \"member_count\": 8,\n  \"task_count\": 45,\n  \"archived\": false,\n  \"visibility\": \"internal\"\n}\n```\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                                     |\n|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|\n| 400         | Bad request - malformed body or invalid values.               |\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                                        |\n| 403         | Forbidden - requires admin or owner on the project.           |\n| 404         | Project not found.                                            |\n\n---\n\n### Delete a project\n\nDeletes a project. By default the deletion cascades: all tasks within the project are deleted as well. This action cannot be undone. Pass `cascade=false` to delete the project only when it contains no tasks.\n\n```plaintext\nDELETE /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/projects/{projectId}`\n\n**Method**: `DELETE`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Owner on the project\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute   | Type    | Required | Description                                                            |\n|-------------|---------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `projectId` | integer | Yes      | The ID of the project to delete.                                         |\n| `cascade`   | boolean | No       | If `true`, deletes all tasks within the project. Default is `true`.      |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --request DELETE \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/projects/3?cascade=false\"\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `204 No Content`\n\nThe response body is empty.\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                                                        |\n|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                                                          |\n| 403         | Forbidden - requires project owner.                                             |\n| 404         | Project not found.                                                              |\n| 409         | Conflict - project still contains tasks and `cascade` was `false`.               |\n\n---\n\n## Users\n\nUse this API to retrieve information about the authenticated user.\n\n### Retrieve the current user\n\nRetrieves the profile of the currently authenticated user, including basic subscription information. Use the `fields` query parameter to request only the attributes you need.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/users/me\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/users/me`\n\n**Method**: `GET`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: None\n\n**Query parameters**\n\n| Attribute | Type   | Required | Description                                                          |\n|-----------|--------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `fields`  | string | No       | Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response. For example, `fields=id,email,name`. |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/users/me?fields=id,email,name,role\"\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `200 OK`\n\n| Attribute          | Type    | Description                                                  |\n|--------------------|---------|---------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `user.id`          | integer | User ID.                                                       |\n| `user.email`       | string  | Account email address.                                         |\n| `user.name`        | string  | Display name.                                                  |\n| `user.role`        | string  | Organization role.                                             |\n| `user.organization_id` | integer | Organization ID.                                            |\n| `user.timezone`    | string  | IANA time zone of the user profile.                            |\n| `user.created_at`  | string  | ISO 8601 account creation timestamp.                           |\n| `user.last_login`  | integer | Legacy Unix timestamp of the last login. Migrates to ISO 8601 in API v3. |\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user\": {\n    \"id\": 57,\n    \"email\": \"jane@example.com\",\n    \"name\": \"Jane Smith\",\n    \"role\": \"admin\",\n    \"organization_id\": 5,\n    \"timezone\": \"America/New_York\",\n    \"created_at\": \"2023-01-15T09:00:00Z\",\n    \"last_login\": 1709398800\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Notes**\n\n- When `fields` is supplied, only the requested attributes are returned. `id` is always returned.\n- `last_login` is a legacy Unix timestamp; see [Timestamps](#timestamps).\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning               |\n|-------------|------------------------|\n| 401         | Authentication failed. |\n\n---\n\n## Search\n\nUse this API to search for tasks.\n\n### Search for tasks\n\nSearches tasks by full-text query, optionally narrowed by project, status, and due-date range.\n\n```plaintext\nGET /api/v2/search/tasks\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/search/tasks`\n\n**Method**: `GET`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Read access to the projects searched\n\n**Query parameters**\n\n| Attribute    | Type    | Required | Description                                                       |\n|--------------|---------|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `q`          | string  | Yes      | Full-text search query. Matches task titles and descriptions.      |\n| `date_from`  | string  | No       | Only return tasks due on or after this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).        |\n| `date_to`    | string  | No       | Only return tasks due on or before this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).       |\n| `project_id` | integer | No       | Restrict the search to this project.                               |\n| `status`     | string  | No       | Restrict the search to this task status.                           |\n\nURL-encode the query value; use `--data-urlencode` in cURL or percent-encoding such as `%20` for spaces.\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --request GET \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --data-urlencode \"q=landing page\" \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/search/tasks?project_id=12&status=open\"\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `200 OK`\n\nReturns task objects with the same attributes as [List all tasks](#list-all-tasks), ordered by relevance:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"data\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": 1107,\n      \"title\": \"Design new landing page\",\n      \"description\": \"Create mockups for the Q2 marketing campaign\",\n      \"status\": \"open\",\n      \"priority\": \"high\",\n      \"assignee_id\": null,\n      \"project_id\": 12,\n      \"created_at\": \"2024-03-05T10:00:00Z\",\n      \"updated_at\": \"2024-03-05T10:00:00Z\",\n      \"due_date\": \"2024-04-01T00:00:00Z\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"meta\": {\n    \"current_page\": 1,\n    \"total_pages\": 1,\n    \"total_count\": 1\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                            |\n|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|\n| 400         | Bad request - `q` missing or a date range is invalid. |\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                               |\n\n---\n\n## Webhooks\n\nUse this API to register and remove webhooks that push TaskFlow events to your integration endpoints. For the full list of event types, payload examples, and delivery semantics, see the [webhook event catalog](webhook_event_catalog.html).\n\n### Create a webhook\n\nRegisters a webhook that receives the selected event types at your webhook URL. Provide an HMAC `secret` so you can verify payload signatures; `active` controls whether the webhook fires immediately after creation.\n\n```plaintext\nPOST /api/v2/webhooks\n```\n\n**URL**: `/api/v2/webhooks`\n\n**Method**: `POST`\n\n**Auth required**: YES\n\n**Permissions required**: Admin or owner on the workspace\n\n**Request attributes**\n\n| Attribute | Type         | Required | Description                                                                                          |\n|-----------|--------------|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| `url`     | string (URI) | Yes      | The webhook URL that receives event payloads. Must be publicly reachable over HTTPS.                   |\n| `events`  | string array | Yes      | Event types to subscribe to. One or more of `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `task.assigned`, `task.commented`, `project.created`, `project.archived`, `project.deleted`, `member.added`, `member.removed`. |\n| `secret`  | string       | No       | HMAC secret used to sign payloads for verification.                                                     |\n| `active`  | boolean      | No       | Whether the webhook is active. Default is `true`.                                                       |\n\n**Example request**\n\n```shell\ncurl --request POST \\\n  --url \"https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/webhooks\" \\\n  --header \"Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>\" \\\n  --header \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data '{\n    \"url\": \"https://integrations.acme.corp/taskflow/events\",\n    \"events\": [\"task.created\", \"task.updated\", \"project.archived\"],\n    \"secret\": \"<your_hmac_secret>\",\n    \"active\": true\n  }'\n```\n\n**Success response**\n\n**Code**: `201 Created`\n\n| Attribute    | Type         | Description                                    |\n|--------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------|\n| `id`         | integer      | Webhook ID.                                     |\n| `url`        | string       | The webhook URL.                                |\n| `events`     | string array | Subscribed event types.                         |\n| `active`     | boolean      | Whether the webhook is active.                  |\n| `created_at` | string       | ISO 8601 creation timestamp.                    |\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": 301,\n  \"url\": \"https://integrations.acme.corp/taskflow/events\",\n  \"events\": [\"task.created\", \"task.updated\", \"project.archived\"],\n  \"active\": true,\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-02-20T11:30:00Z\"\n}\n```\n\n**Error responses**\n\n| Status code | Meaning                                                        |\n|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|\n| 400         | Bad request - malformed body.                                    |\n| 401         | Authentication failed.                                           |\n| 422         | Validation error - `url` not reachable/valid, or unknown event type. |\n\n**Notes**\n\n- **Payload verification.** When a `secret` is configured, each delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 and the signature is sent in the `X-TaskFlow-Signature` header. Verify it before trusting a payload.\n- **Retry policy.** A delivery that does not return a `2xx` status is retried up to 3 times with exponential backoff. If all attempts fail, the delivery is marked `failed` and is not retried again. Production logs confirm this behavior (a `project.deleted` delivery returned `502` and was retired after 3 attempts).\n- **Event types.** The declared subscription list is the ten event types above. 1: # TaskFlow API Documentation
2: 
3: **Version**: 2.0
4: **Last Updated**: March 2024
5: 
6: Welcome to the TaskFlow API! This document describes how to interact with our REST API for managing tasks and projects. You can use these endpoints to build integrations with TaskFlow.
7: 
8: ## Authentication
9: 
10: All API calls require a valid API key. Include your key in the `Authorization` header:
11: 
12: ```
13: Authorization: Bearer <your_api_key>
14: ```
15: 
16: You can generate an API key from the TaskFlow dashboard under Settings > API Keys.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## Tasks
21: 
22: ### GET /api/v2/tasks
23: 
24: Retrieves a list of tasks for the authenticated user. The user can filter results using query parameters.
25: 
26: **Query Parameters**
27: 
28: | Parameter | Type | Description |
29: |-----------|------|-------------|
30: | status | string | Filter by task status. Allowed values: `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived` |
31: | project_id | integer | Only return tasks belonging to this project |
32: | page | integer | Page number for pagination (default: 1) |
33: | per_page | integer | Number of results per page (default: 20, max: 100) |
34: | sort | string | Sort field. One of `created_at`, `updated_at`, `priority` |
35: | order | string | Sort direction: `asc` or `desc` |
36: 
37: **Example Request**
38: 
39: ```bash
40: curl -X GET "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks?status=open&page=1" \
41:   -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
42: ```
43: 
44: **Response** (200 OK)
45: 
46: ```json
47: {
48:   "data": [
49:     {
50:       "id": 1042,
51:       "title": "Fix login bug",
52:       "description": "Users are unable to login with SSO",
53:       "status": "open",
54:       "priority": "high",
55:       "assignee_id": 57,
56:       "project_id": 12,
57:       "created_at": "2024-03-01T14:22:00Z",
58:       "updated_at": "2024-03-01T14:22:00Z",
59:       "due_date": "2024-03-15T00:00:00Z"
60:     }
61:   ],
62:   "meta": {
63:     "current_page": 1,
64:     "total_pages": 5,
65:     "total_count": 98
66:   }
67: }
68: ```
69: 
70: ---
71: 
72: ### POST /api/v2/tasks
73: 
74: Creates a new task. You must provide at least a title. The task will be created under the user's default project if `project_id` is not specified.
75: 
76: **Request Body Arguments**
77: 
78: - `title` (string, **required**) - The title of the task. Max 255 characters.
79: - `description` (string) - A longer description. Supports Markdown formatting.
80: - `status` (string) - Initial status. Defaults to `open`.
81: - `priority` (string) - One of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`. Default is `medium`.
82: - `assignee_id` (integer) - User ID to assign the task to.
83: - `project_id` (integer) - Project to create the task in.
84: - `due_date` (string) - Due date in ISO 8601 format.
85: - `tags` (array of strings) - Tags to apply to the task.
86: 
87: **Example**
88: 
89: ```python
90: import requests
91: 
92: resp = requests.post(
93:     "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks",
94:     headers={"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"},
95:     json={
96:         "title": "Design new landing page",
97:         "description": "Create mockups for the Q2 marketing campaign",
98:         "priority": "high",
99:         "project_id": 12,
100:         "due_date": "2024-04-01T00:00:00Z",
101:         "tags": ["design", "marketing"]
102:     }
103: )
104: print(resp.json())
105: ```
106: 
107: Returns `201 Created` on success with the full task object in the response body.
108: 
109: **Errors**
110: 
111: | Status Code | Meaning |
112: |------------|---------|
113: | 400 | Bad request - missing required fields or invalid values |
114: | 401 | Authentication failed |
115: | 422 | Validation error (e.g. title too long) |
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ### GET /api/v2/tasks/{id}
120: 
121: Get a single task by its ID.
122: 
123: Pass the task ID as a path parameter. Returns the task object if found. Returns 404 if the task doesn't exist or you don't have access.
124: 
125: Response includes the full task object (same schema as list endpoint).
126: 
127: No additional arguments.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ### Updating a task - PUT /api/v2/tasks/{id}
132: 
133: We support partial updates - you only need to send the fields you want to change. Any fields not included in the request body will remain unchanged.
134: 
135: Note: the `id` and `created_at` fields cannot be modified.
136: 
137: **Fields you can update:**
138: 
139: - title
140: - description
141: - status (must be a valid status string)
142: - priority
143: - assignee_id (set to `null` to unassign)
144: - project_id
145: - due_date (ISO 8601 timestamp or null to clear)
146: - tags
147: 
148: **Sample curl command:**
149: 
150: ```bash
151: curl -X PUT "https://api.taskflow.io/api/v2/tasks/1042" \
152:   -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
153:   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
154:   -d '{"status": "in_progress", "assignee_id": 57}'
155: ```
156: 
157: The API returns `200 OK` and the updated task object on success.
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ### DELETE /api/v2/tasks/{id}
162: 
163: Permanently deletes a task. This action cannot be undone.
164: 
165: The user must have admin or owner permissions on the project that the task belongs to. Regular members can only delete tasks they created.
166: 
167: **Returns:**
168: 
169: `204 No Content` on success. The response body is empty.
170: 
171: If the task is not found a `404` error is returned. Attempting to delete a task without sufficient permissions results in `403 Forbidden`.
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## Projects
176: 
177: ### List projects
178: 
179: ```
180: GET /api/v2/projects
181: ```
182: 
183: This route returns all projects the authenticated user has access to. Projects are returned in alphabetical order by name.
184: 
185: **Query args:**
186: 
187: - `archived` (boolean) - if `true`, include archived projects. Default `false`.
188: - `role` (string) - filter by the user's role in the project: `owner`, `admin`, `member`
189: 
190: No authentication header examples are given here since it follows the same pattern described at the top of this doc.
191: 
192: **Sample response:**
193: 
194: ```json
195: {
196:   "projects": [
197:     {
198:       "id": 12,
199:       "name": "Website Redesign",
200:       "description": "Q2 2024 website overhaul",
201:       "owner_id": 57,
202:       "created": 1709312400,
203:       "member_count": 8,
204:       "task_count": 45,
205:       "archived": false
206:     }
207:   ]
208: }
209: ```
210: 
211: Note that the `created` field here returns a Unix timestamp. We plan to migrate this to ISO 8601 in a future release.
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ### Create Project
216: 
217: **Endpoint:** `POST /api/v2/projects`
218: 
219: To create a new project, send a POST request with the following payload:
220: 
221: ```json
222: {
223:   "name": "My New Project",
224:   "description": "Optional project description"
225: }
226: ```
227: 
228: The `name` field is required and must be unique within the user's organization. Max 100 chars.
229: 
230: **Response fields:**
231: 
232: | Field | Type | Notes |
233: |-------|------|-------|
234: | id | integer | Auto-generated project ID |
235: | name | string | The project name |
236: | description | string | May be null |
237: | owner_id | integer | ID of creating user |
238: | created | integer | Unix timestamp |
239: | member_count | integer | Always 1 for new projects |
240: | task_count | integer | Always 0 for new projects |
241: | archived | boolean | Always false for new projects |
242: 
243: Returns HTTP 201.
244: 
245: No error documentation is provided here but the API follows standard REST conventions for error responses.
246: 
247: ---
248: 
249: ## User Info
250: 
251: ### Getting your profile
252: 
253: **Route**: GET /api/v2/users/me
254: 
255: This returns information about the currently authenticated user. Pass your API key as usual.
256: 
257: The response looks like:
258: 
259: ```json
260: {
261:   "user": {
262:     "id": 57,
263:     "email": "jane@example.com",
264:     "name": "Jane Smith",
265:     "role": "admin",
266:     "organization_id": 5,
267:     "timezone": "America/New_York",
268:     "created_at": "2023-01-15T09:00:00Z",
269:     "last_login": 1709398800
270:   }
271: }
272: ```
273: 
274: Note: `created_at` is ISO 8601 but `last_login` is a Unix timestamp. This inconsistency will be addressed in API v3.
275: 
276: ---
277: 
278: ## Rate Limiting
279: 
280: We enforce rate limits to ensure fair usage of the API. The current limits are:
281: 
282: - 100 requests per minute for free tier
283: - 1000 requests per minute for paid plans
284: 
285: When you exceed the limit, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Check the `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header to see how many requests you have left.
286: 
287: ## Pagination
288: 
289: List endpoints support pagination via `page` and `per_page` query parameters. The response `meta` object contains pagination info. Note that the projects endpoint does not currently support pagination - all projects are returned in a single response.
290: 
291: ## Errors
292: 
293: The API uses standard HTTP status codes. Error responses include a JSON body:
294: 
295: ```json
296: {
297:   "error": {
298:     "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
299:     "message": "Title is required",
300:     "details": []
301:   }
302: }
303: ```
304: 
305: However, some older endpoints may return errors in a different format:
306: 
307: ```json
308: {
309:   "error": "not_found",
310:   "message": "Task not found"
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: We are working on standardizing error responses across all routes.
315: 
316: ---
317: 
318: *For questions or support, email api-support@taskflow.io*

(End of file - total 318 lines)

1: # TaskFlow API v1
2: 
3: API base URL: `https://api.taskflow.io/api`
4: 
5: Auth: use `X-API-Key` header with your key.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## GET /api/tasks
10: 
11: Gets tasks. Returns JSON array.
12: 
13: Params: `status`, `project`, `limit`, `offset`
14: 
15: Response: array of task objects.
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## POST /api/tasks
20: 
21: Create a task.
22: 
23: Body: JSON with `title` (required), `desc`, `status`, `priority`, `assigned_to`, `project`, `deadline`.
24: 
25: `deadline` should be a Unix timestamp.
26: 
27: Returns the created task. 200 OK.
28: 
29: ---
30: 
31: ## GET /api/tasks/:id
32: 
33: Fetch one task.
34: 
35: ---
36: 
37: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id
38: 
39: Update task fields. Send only what changed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## DELETE /api/tasks/:id
44: 
45: Delete a task. Must be owner.
46: 
47: ---
48: 
49: ## GET /api/projects
50: 
51: List all projects.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## POST /api/projects
56: 
57: Make a new project. Body: `name` (required), `desc`.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## GET /api/users/current
62: 
63: Get current user info.
64: 
65: Response:
66: 
67: ```
68: {
69:   "id": 57,
70:   "email": "jane@example.com",
71:   "name": "Jane Smith",
72:   "role": "admin",
73:   "org": 5
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/comments
80: 
81: List comments on a task.
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## POST /api/tasks/:id/comments
86: 
87: Add comment. Body: `text`.
88: 
89: ---
90: 
91: ## GET /api/search
92: 
93: Search across tasks and projects.
94: 
95: Params: `q` (search query), `type` (task or project)
96: 
97: ---
98: 
99: ## PUT /api/tasks/:id/assign
100: 
101: Assign a task to a user. Body: `user_id`.
102: 
103: This is a convenience endpoint. You can also update the `assigned_to` field directly via PUT /api/tasks/:id.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## GET /api/tasks/:id/history
108: 
109: Returns change history for a task. Each entry shows what field changed, old value, new value, who changed it, and when (Unix timestamp).
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## DELETE /api/projects/:id
114: 
115: Delete a project. All tasks in the project will also be deleted.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Errors
120: 
121: Errors return JSON: `{"error": "message"}`.
122: 
123: Common codes: 400, 401, 404, 500.
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Webhooks
128: 
129: POST /api/webhooks - register a webhook. Body: `url`, `events` (array).
130: 
131: GET /api/webhooks - list webhooks.
132: 
133: DELETE /api/webhooks/:id - remove a webhook.
134: 
135: Events: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.deleted`, `project.created`.
136: 
137: ---
138: 
139: ## Notes
140: 
141: - Rate limit: 60 req/min.
142: - All timestamps are Unix.
143: - Contact support@taskflow.io for help.

(End of file - total 143 lines)
</content>", "type": "text"}]

1: ---
2: stage: none
3: group: unassigned
4: info: For assistance with this Style Guide page, see <https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/product/ux/technical-writing/#assignments-to-other-projects-and-subjects>.
5: description: Writing styles, markup, formatting, and other standards for the GitLab RESTful APIs.
6: title: Documenting REST API resources
7: ---
8: 
9: REST API resources are documented in Markdown under
10: [`/doc/api`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/tree/master/doc/api). Each
11: resource has its own Markdown file, which is linked from
12: [`api_resources.md`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/doc/api/api_resources.md).
13: 
14: When modifying the Markdown or API code, also update the corresponding
15: [OpenAPI definition](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/tree/master/doc/api/openapi), by running
16: `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v2:generate` and `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v3:generate`.
17: To check if the OpenAPI definition needs to be updated, you can run `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v2:check_docs` and
18: `bin/rake gitlab:openapi:v3:check_docs`.
19: This is also checked by the `openapi-doc-check` CI/CD job that runs for commits that modify API code or documentation.
20: 
21: The Markdown topic for an API resource must include:
22: 
23: - A block that includes the HTTP method (like GET, PUT, DELETE) followed by the request path. Always start the path with a `/`. For example:
24: 
25:   ```plaintext
26:   GET /api/v4/projects/:id/repository/branches
27:   ```
28: 
29: - A detailed [description of the attributes](#request-attributes).
30: - A detailed [description of the response body](#response-attributes).
31: - A cURL example.
32: - A response body example (in JSON format).
33: 
34: After a new API documentation page is added, [add an entry in the global navigation](site_architecture/global_nav.md#add-a-navigation-entry).
35: 
36: ## Page metadata
37: 
38: When you create a new page, include a `description` metadata field
39: in the front matter that follows these guidelines for consistency:
40: 
41: - Start with "REST API to"
42: - Use action verbs that describe what users can do with the API
43: - Avoid words ending in -ing
44: - Keep to one sentence, ideally under 100 characters
45: - End with a period
46: 
47: For example:
48: 
49: ```yaml
50: ---
51: stage: Example Stage
52: group: Example Group
53: info: To determine the technical writer assigned to the Stage/Group associated with this page, see <https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/product/ux/technical-writing/#assignments>
54: description: REST API to create, update, and delete issues.
55: title: Example page title
56: ---
57: ```
58: 
59: Additional examples:
60: 
61: - `description: REST API to retrieve CI/CD job details, retry and cancel jobs, run manual jobs, and access job logs.`
62: - `description: REST API to create, manage, and monitor CI/CD pipelines.`
63: 
64: ## API topic template
65: 
66: Use the following template to help you get started. Be sure to list any
67: required attributes first in the table.
68: 
69: ````markdown
70: ## API name
71: 
72: {{</* history */>}}
73: 
74: - History note.
75: 
76: {{</* /history */>}}
77: 
78: Use this API to ...
79: 
80: ### Operation title
81: 
82: {{</* history */>}}
83: 
84: - History note.
85: 
86: {{</* /history */>}}
87: 
88: Description of the operation.
89: 
90: ```plaintext
91: METHOD /api/v4/endpoint
92: ```
93: 
94: Supported attributes:
95: 
96: | Attribute                | Type     | Required | Description           |
97: |--------------------------|----------|----------|-----------------------|
98: | `attribute`              | datatype | Yes      | Detailed description. |
99: | `attribute`              | datatype | No       | Detailed description. |
100: | `attribute`              | datatype | No       | Detailed description. |
101: | `attribute`              | datatype | No       | Detailed description. |
102: 
103: If successful, returns [`<status_code>`](rest/troubleshooting.md#status-codes) and the following
104: response attributes:
105: 
106: | Attribute                | Type     | Description           |
107: |--------------------------|----------|-----------------------|
108: | `attribute`              | datatype | Detailed description. |
109: | `attribute`              | datatype | Detailed description. |
110: 
111: Example request:
112: 
113: ```shell
114: curl --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
115:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/endpoint?parameters"
116: ```
117: 
118: Example response:
119: 
120: ```json
121: [
122:   {
123:   }
124: ]
125: ```
126: ````
127: 
128: ## History
129: 
130: Add [history](styleguide/availability_details.md#history)
131: to describe new or updated API calls.
132: 
133: To add history for an individual attribute, include it in the history
134: for the section. For example:
135: 
136: ```markdown
137: ### Edit a widget
138: 
139: {{</* history */>}}
140: 
141:  - `widget_message` [introduced](https://link-to-issue) in GitLab 14.3.
142: 
143: {{</* /history */>}}
144: ```
145: 
146: If the API or attribute is deployed behind a feature flag,
147: [include the feature flag information](feature_flags.md) in the history.
148: 
149: ## Deprecations
150: 
151: To document the deprecation of an API endpoint, follow the steps to
152: [deprecate a page or topic](styleguide/deprecations_and_removals.md).
153: 
154: To deprecate an attribute:
155: 
156: 1. Add a history note.
157: 
158:    ```markdown
159:    {{</* history */>}}
160: 
161:    - `widget_name` [deprecated](https://link-to-issue) in GitLab 14.7.
162: 
163:    {{</* /history */>}}
164:    ```
165: 
166: 1. Add inline deprecation text to the description.
167: 
168:    ```markdown
169:    | Attribute     | Type   | Required | Description |
170:    |---------------|--------|----------|-------------|
171:    | `widget_name` | string | No       | [Deprecated](https://link-to-issue) in GitLab 14.7. Use `widget_id` instead. The name of the widget. |
172:    ```
173: 
174: To widely announce a deprecation, [update the REST API deprecations page](../../api/rest/deprecations.md).
175: 
176: ## API introduction
177: 
178: Each API is made of one or more operations. At the start of the topic, include information that
179: applies to all operations in the API, and a short description of the related features.
180: 
181: For consistency, try to start the introduction with: `Use this API to {verb} + [{feature}](link/to/UI/docs).`
182: This allows us to direct users to related documentation that might include more context.
183: 
184: For example:
185: 
186: - `Use this API to manage [Git branches](path/to/file).`
187: - `Use this API to interact with the [Maven package manager client](path/to/file).`
188: - `Use this API to interact with namespaces, a special resource category used to organize users and groups. For more information, see [namespaces](path/to/file).`
189: 
190: ## Operation titles
191: 
192: Start an operation title with a verb. For consistency,
193: use these verbs based on the HTTP method:
194: 
195: | HTTP method      | Verb     | Alternatives | Examples |
196: | ---------------- | -------- | ------------ | -------- |
197: | `GET` (multiple) | List all |              | `List all group access tokens` |
198: | `GET` (single)   | Retrieve | Download     | `Retrieve a group audit event`, `Download a dependency list export` |
199: | `POST`           | Create   | Add          | `Create a repository branch`, `Add a new emoji reaction` |
200: | `PUT`            | Update   | Replace      | `Update a project topic` |
201: | `PATCH`          | Update   | Modify       | `Update a freeze period`, `Modify an existing commit thread note` |
202: | `DELETE`         | Delete   |              | `Delete a feature` |
203: 
204: When possible, use the recommended verb. Alternatives might be needed in specific contexts, but
205: minimize their use to maintain consistency.
206: 
207: ## Operation descriptions
208: 
209: Each operation should include a short description that explains its use, and highlights any
210: important information. If possible, write the first sentence to broadly repeat the title of
211: the operation. For example:
212: 
213: - `List all project access tokens` -> `Lists all project access tokens.`
214: - `Delete an SSH key` -> `Deletes an SSH key from your user account.`
215: - `Retrieve an enterprise user` -> `Retrieves details on a specified enterprise user.`
216: 
217: ## Request attributes
218: 
219: You must document the request attributes in an operation. When creating the table and attribute descriptions:
220: 
221: - Use the following column names for attribute tables.
222: - List any path attributes first, then any required attributes, then sort alphabetically.
223: - Place the attribute name in code blocks using backticks (`` ` ``).
224: - Document any tier or offering information specific to an attribute in the description.
225:   - If an attribute is available for Premium, mention that it's also available for Ultimate.
226:   - Combine this tier and offering information when possible. For example: `GitLab Self-Managed, Premium and Ultimate only.`
227: 
228: ```markdown
229: | Attribute                    | Type          | Required | Description                                         |
230: |------------------------------|---------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
231: | `title`                      | string        | Yes      | Title of the issue. GitLab Self-Managed only.       |
232: | `assignee_ids`               | integer array | No       | IDs of the users to assign the issue to. Ultimate only. |
233: | `confidential`               | boolean       | No       | Sets the issue to confidential. Default is `false`. |
234: ```
235: 
236: Rendered example:
237: 
238: | Attribute                    | Type          | Required | Description                                         |
239: |------------------------------|---------------|----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
240: | `title`                      | string        | Yes      | Title of the issue. GitLab Self-Managed only.       |
241: | `assignee_ids`               | integer array | No       | IDs of the users to assign the issue to. Ultimate only. |
242: | `confidential`               | boolean       | No       | Sets the issue to confidential. Default is `false`. |
243: 
244: For information about writing attribute descriptions, see the [GraphQL API description style guide](../api_graphql_styleguide.md#description-style-guide).
245: 
246: ### Conditionally required attributes
247: 
248: If an attribute is related to another item, indicate this in the attribute description.
249: 
250: Generally, this happens if one of two attributes is required or if an attribute must be enabled and configured separately.
251: 
252: First define the attribute itself, then mention any requirements. Use this format:
253: 
254:   ```markdown
255:   Required if `attribute1` is `true`.
256:   ```
257: 
258: For example:
259: 
260: | Attribute                  | Type    | Required    | Description |
261: | -------------------------- | ------- | ----------- | ----------- |
262: | `include_saml_users`       | boolean | Conditional | If `true`, returns users with a SAML identity. Required if `include_service_accounts` is `false`. |
263: | `include_service_accounts` | boolean | Conditional | If `true`, returns service account users. Required if `include_saml_users` is `false`. |
264: | `a_related_setting`        | boolean | Conditional | If `true`, does something else. Required if `include_saml_users` is `true`. |
265: 
266: ## Response attributes
267: 
268: You might sometimes need to document the response attributes in an operation. This is not usually required.
269: When creating the table and attribute descriptions:
270: 
271: - Use the following column names for attribute tables.
272: - Sort the table alphabetically.
273: - Place the attribute name in code blocks using backticks (`` ` ``).
274: - If describing an object or array, use dot notation to represent the sub-attributes. For example, `project.name` or `projects[].name`.
275: - Document any tier or offering information specific to an attribute in the description.
276:   - If an attribute is available for Premium, mention that it's also available for Ultimate.
277:   - Combine this tier and offering information when possible. For example: `GitLab Self-Managed, Premium and Ultimate only.`
278: 
279: Start the description with the following sentence, replacing `status code` with the
280: relevant [HTTP status code](../../api/rest/troubleshooting.md#status-codes), for example:
281: 
282: ```markdown
283: If successful, returns [`200 OK`](../../api/rest/troubleshooting.md#status-codes) and the
284: following response attributes:
285: ```
286: 
287: ```markdown
288: | Attribute      | Type          | Description |
289: | -------------- | ------------- | ----------- |
290: | `assignee_ids` | integer array | IDs of the users to assign the issue to. Premium and Ultimate only. |
291: | `commits`      | object array  | Commits in the merge request diff. |
292: | `commits[].id` | string        | ID of the commit. |
293: ```
294: 
295: Rendered example:
296: 
297: | Attribute      | Type          | Description |
298: | -------------- | ------------- | ----------- |
299: | `assignee_ids` | integer array | IDs of the users to assign the issue to. Premium and Ultimate only. |
300: | `commits`      | object array  | Commits in the merge request diff. |
301: | `commits[].id` | string        | ID of the commit. |
302: 
303: For information about writing attribute descriptions, see the [GraphQL API description style guide](../api_graphql_styleguide.md#description-style-guide).
304: 
305: ## cURL commands
306: 
307: - Use `https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/` as an endpoint.
308: - Wherever needed use this personal access token: `<your_access_token>`.
309: - Always put the request first. `GET` is the default so you don't have to
310:   include it.
311: - Use long option names (`--header` instead of `-H`) for legibility. (Tested in
312:   [`scripts/lint-doc.sh`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/scripts/lint-doc.sh).)
313: - Declare URLs with the `--url` parameter, and wrap the URL in double quotes (`"`).
314: - Prefer to use examples using the personal access token and don't pass data of
315:   username and password.
316: - For legibility, use the ` \ ` character and indentation to break long single-line
317:   commands apart into multiple lines.
318: 
319: | Methods                                         | Description                                            |
320: |-------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
321: | `--header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>"` | Use this method as is, whenever authentication needed. |

326: ## cURL Examples
327: 
328: The following sections include a set of [cURL](https://curl.se/) examples
329: you can use in the API documentation.
330: 
331: > [!warning]
332: > Do not use information for real users, URLs, or tokens. For documentation, refer to our
333: > relevant style guide sections on [fake user information](styleguide/_index.md#fake-user-information),
334: > [fake URLs](styleguide/_index.md#fake-urls), and [fake tokens](styleguide/_index.md#fake-tokens).
335: 
336: ### Simple cURL command
337: 
338: Get the details of a group:
339: 
340: ```shell
341: curl --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
342:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/groups/gitlab-org"
343: ```
344: 
345: ### cURL example with parameters passed in the URL
346: 
347: Create a new project under the authenticated user's namespace:
348: 
349: ```shell
350: curl --request POST --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
351:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects?name=foo"
352: ```
353: 
354: ### Post data using cURL's `--data`
355: 
356: Instead of using `--request POST` and appending the parameters to the URI, you
357: can use cURL's `--data` option. The example below creates a new project
358: `foo` under the authenticated user's namespace.
359: 
360: ```shell
361: curl --data "name=foo" \
362:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
363:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects"
364: ```
365: 
366: ### Post data using cURL's `--data-urlencode`
367: 
368: Use `--data-urlencode` when the data contains special characters that require URL encoding.
369: 
370: You can use this option for:
371: 
372: - Markdown content with code blocks or special formatting.
373: - Regular expressions containing `+`, `.`, or `*`.
374: - Text with quotes, ampersands, or other reserved URL characters.
375: - File content that might contain special characters.
376: 
377: For alphanumeric data without special characters, use [`--data`](#post-data-using-curls---data) instead.
378: 
379: For an attribute with special characters:
380: 
381: ```shell
382: curl --request POST \
383:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
384:   --data-urlencode "description=Fix issue with 'quotes' & ampersands" \
385:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/1/issues"
386: ```
387: 
388: For content with regular expression patterns:
389: 
390: ```shell
391: curl --request DELETE \
392:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
393:   --data-urlencode "name_regex_delete=dev-.+" \
394:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/5/registry/repositories/2/tags"
395: ```
396: 
397: For content from a file, use `attribute@filename`:
398: 
399: ```shell
400: curl --request POST \
401:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
402:   --data-urlencode "title=API documentation update" \
403:   --data-urlencode "content@content.md" \
404:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/1/wikis"
405: ```
406: 
407: ### Post data using JSON content
408: 
409: This example creates a new group. Be aware of the use of single (`'`) and double
410: (`"`) quotes.
411: 
412: ```shell
413: curl --request POST \
414:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
415:   --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
416:   --data '{"path": "my-group", "name": "My group"}' \
417:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/groups"
418: ```
419: 
420: For readability, you can also set up the `--data` by using the following format:
421: 
422: ```shell
423: curl --request POST \
424:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/groups" \
425:   --header "content-type: application/json" \
426:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
427:   --data '{
428:     "path": "my-group",
429:     "name": "My group"
430: }'
431: ```
432: 
433: ### Post data using form-data
434: 
435: Instead of using JSON or URL-encoding data, you can use `multipart/form-data` which
436: properly handles data encoding:
437: 
438: ```shell
439: curl --request POST \
440:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
441:   --form "title=ssh-key" \
442:   --form "key=ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EA..." \
443:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/users/25/keys"
444: ```
445: 
446: The above example adds an SSH public key titled `ssh-key` to the account of
447: a user with ID 25. The operation requires administrator access.
448: 
449: ### Escape special characters
450: 
451: Spaces or slashes (`/`) can sometimes result in errors, so you should
452: escape them when possible. In the example below we create a new issue which
453: contains spaces in its title. Observe how spaces are escaped using the `%20`
454: ASCII code.
455: 
456: ```shell
457: curl --request POST \
458:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>" \
459:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/42/issues?title=Hello%20GitLab"
460: ```
461: 
462: Use `%2F` for slashes (`/`).
463: 
464: ### Pass arrays to API calls
465: 
466: The GitLab API sometimes accepts arrays of strings or integers. For example, to
467: exclude specific users when requesting a list of users for a project, you would
468: do something like this:
469: 
470: ```shell
471: curl --request PUT \
472:   --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <your_access_token>"
473:   --data "skip_users[]=<user_id>" \
474:   --data "skip_users[]=<user_id>" \
475:   --url "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/<project_id>/users"
476: ```

[{"type": "text"}, {"id": "e069a63f-1ba8-4add-9b94-e4f190ec2689", "name": "write", "arguments": "{\"filePath\":\"/work/output/taskflow_api_style_guide.md\",\"content\":\"# TaskFlow API Documentation Style Guide\\n\\n**Version:** 1.0\\n**Applies to:** All TaskFlow REST API documentation (v2 and later)\\n**Maintained by:** Technical Writing, Developer Experience\\n**Based on:** The TaskFlow RESTAPIDocs endpoint template, the per-endpoint documentation audit rubric, the OpenAPI 3.0 extract for the platform API, and the REST API documentation conventions used by mature open-source projects such as GitLab.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. Purpose and scope\\n\\nThis guide governs how TaskFlow writes, structures, and maintains REST API documentation. It applies to every Markdown topic published under the TaskFlow API documentation set: endpoint references, authentication guides, webhook catalogs, migration guides, and any future API version. Its goal is to make every endpoint page predictable: a developer who has read one TaskFlow endpoint should be able to read any other one without relearning the layout, the vocabulary, or the tone.\\n\\nTwo truths drive the rules below. First, our documentation has historically been written ad hoc by multiple engineers, and the audit trail shows the costs: inconsistent terminology, missing authentication notes, empty error tables, and endpoints that exist in the codebase but not on the page. Second, we maintain an OpenAPI 3.0 specification extracted from the codebase, and that specification is machine-checkable in a way prose is not. The specification therefore anchors the facts; the prose adds the judgment, context, and examples that a schema cannot carry.\\n\\n## 2. Source-of-truth hierarchy\\n\\nWhen sources disagree, resolve them in this order and record the decision in the discrepancy report:\\n\\n1. **The OpenAPI specification.** For anything a machine can verify \u2014 paths, methods, parameter names, parameter types, enums, defaults, maximums, required flags, declared response codes \u2014 the spec wins. Example: the spec enforces `maxLength: 200` on task titles, so any document that says \\\"max 255 characters\\\" is wrong regardless of how long it has said so.\\n2. **The current endpoint documentation.** For behavioral statements the spec does not express \u2014 sort order, cascade behavior descriptions, Markdown support in a field, permission rules \u2014 the documentation is the source of truth *unless* it is contradicted by the spec or flagged in the audit tracker. If we keep a documentation-only claim, we file a ticket to backfill it into the spec.\\n3. **The audit tracker.** The tracker records findings a mechanical diff cannot see: description quality, terminology drift, missing authentication notes, and stale sections. Any endpoint marked `needs_rewrite` is rewritten in full, not patched. Any endpoint marked `needs_update` must resolve every note in its row.\\n4. **Production evidence.** For behavior observable only at runtime \u2014 webhook retry counts, observed event types \u2014 the production delivery log is admissible evidence. Document observed behavior and mark it as observed, then reconcile it with the declared spec.\\n\\nNever silently reconcile. Every disagreement between sources gets a row in the discrepancy report with a resolution, even when the resolution is \\\"docs are right, spec must change.\\\"\\n\\n## 3. Page structure\\n\\nEvery endpoint reference follows the structure of the RESTAPIDocs template, extended with the conventions below. A complete operation entry contains, in this order:\\n\\n1. **Operation title** (see \u00a74).\\n2. **Method and path block** \u2014 the HTTP method followed by the full path, in a fenced `plaintext` block, with the path starting with `/`:\\n\\n   ```plaintext\\n   DELETE /api/v2/projects/{projectId}\\n   ```\\n\\n3. **Description** (see \u00a75).\\n4. **Metadata line set** from the template: `URL`, `Method`, `Auth required`, `Permissions required`.\\n5. **Request attributes table** (see \u00a76).\\n6. **Example request** (see \u00a77).\\n7. **Success response** \u2014 the status code, a response attributes table when the body has structure, and one or more example response bodies (see \u00a78).\\n8. **Error responses table** (see \u00a79).\\n9. **Notes** \u2014 anything a developer must know that does not fit above: defaults with caveats, deprecation warnings, retry behavior, rate-limit implications.\\n\\nResource-level introductions (for example, the Tasks chapter) start with one sentence in this pattern: **\\\"Use this API to {verb} {feature}.\\\"** This mirrors the introductions used by GitLab's REST API docs and gives readers an immediate purpose statement before the operations begin.\\n\\n## 4. Operation titles\\n\\nStart every operation title with a verb. Use the verb that matches the HTTP method, per the GitLab convention table, and use the same verb in the title and the first sentence of the description:\\n\\n| HTTP method | Title verb | Example title |\\n|-------------|-----------|---------------|\\n| `GET` (collection) | List all | `List all tasks` |\\n| `GET` (single item) | Retrieve | `Retrieve a task` |\\n| `POST` | Create | `Create a task` |\\n| `PUT` | Update | `Update a task` |\\n| `DELETE` | Delete | `Delete a task` |\\n\\nDo not mix verbs across a page: an endpoint titled \\\"Update a task\\\" must not describe itself as \\\"modifying\\\" the task in the body, and a project section must not drift from \\\"create\\\" to \\\"add\\\" to \\\"register\\\" mid-paragraph. The audit tracker flagged this exact drift repeatedly; it is the single most common quality defect in our legacy docs.\\n\\n## 5. Descriptions\\n\\nWrite a short description for every operation. The first sentence broadly restates the title, in the present tense, third person:\\n\\n- Title: `List all tasks` \u2192 \\\"Lists all tasks the authenticated user can access.\\\"\\n- Title: `Delete a task` \u2192 \\\"Deletes a task permanently.\\\"\\n\\nAfter the first sentence, add only what changes a developer's implementation: permission requirements, defaults, side effects (such as cascade deletion), partial-update semantics, and rate-limit implications. Do not narrate the obvious (\\\"this endpoint takes an ID and returns a task\\\"). Do not promise roadmap behavior in operative sentences; if a change is planned (for example, Unix-to-ISO 8601 migration), state it once in a Note with the target version.\\n\\n## 6. Attribute tables\\n\\nDocument every parameter and every structured response field in a Markdown table. Never describe parameters in loose bullets in a reference page; bullets are permitted in conceptual guides only.\\n\\n**Request attribute tables** use these columns: `Attribute`, `Type`, `Required`, `Description`.\\n\\n- Place path attributes first, then required attributes, then the remaining attributes alphabetically.\\n- Put every attribute name in backticks.\\n- State enums inline with backticked values: One of `open`, `in_progress`, `done`, `archived`, `blocked`.\\n- State defaults explicitly: \\\"Default is `25`.\\\"\\n- State maximums explicitly: \\\"Maximum is `200`.\\\"\\n- For conditionally required attributes, use `Conditional` in the Required column and name the condition: \\\"Required if `include_service_accounts` is `false`.\\\"\\n- Use the parameter names from the OpenAPI specification exactly. 7: Where full URLs are provided in responses they will be rendered as if service
8: is running on 'http://testserver/'.
9: 
10: ## Open Endpoints
11: 
12: Open endpoints require no Authentication.
13: 
14: * [Login](login.md) : `POST /api/login/`
15: 
16: ## Endpoints that require Authentication
17: 
18: Closed endpoints require a valid Token to be included in the header of the
19: request. A Token can be acquired from the Login view above.
20: 
21: ### Current User related
22: 
23: Each endpoint manipulates or displays information related to the User whose
24: Token is provided with the request:
25: 
26: * [Show info](user/get.md) : `GET /api/user/`
27: * [Update info](user/put.md) : `PUT /api/user/`
28: 
29: ### Account related
30: 
31: Endpoints for viewing and manipulating the Accounts that the Authenticated User
32: has permissions to access.
33: 
34: * [Show Accessible Accounts](accounts/get.md) : `GET /api/accounts/`
35: * [Create Account](accounts/post.md) : `POST /api/accounts/`
36: * [Show An Account](accounts/pk/get.md) : `GET /api/accounts/:pk/`
37: * [Update An Account](accounts/pk/put.md) : `PUT /api/accounts/:pk/`
38: * [Delete An Account](accounts/pk/delete.md) : `DELETE /api/accounts/:pk/`
39: # Show Current User
40: 
41: Get the details of the currently Authenticated User along with basic
42: subscription information.
43: 
44: **URL** : `/api/user/`
45: 
46: **Method** : `GET`
47: 
48: **Auth required** : YES
49: 
50: **Permissions required** : None
51: 
52: ## Success Response
53: 
54: **Code** : `200 OK`
55: 
56: **Content examples**

58: For a User with ID 1234 on the local database where that User has saved an

77:     "email": ""
